items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 音乐会厅完成了两小时无脚本独奏即兴，录音后混入人声采样、打击乐、循环音轨、田野录音与拾得音效，形成这张《Sendas》（意为「路径」）。作品延续了他「不重复自身」的创作信条——2021年疫情封锁期间，婚姻的终结与米兰演出取消意外促成了这场录制。Sosa 将爵士、古典、拉丁传统与电子质感熔于一炉，刻意回避风格归类，追求即兴中的「第一遍即定稿」。评论以他本人的创作哲学为核心，强调音乐应回应人类精神迷失的时代背景，并承载喉音唱法般的低频共振意象。整体呈现为独奏钢琴为主导、辅以环境与电子元素点缀的跨界即兴之作。

items._cn_summary: 本文是The Quietus的Rum Music十月专栏，由BBC Radio 3主持人Kate Molleson客座撰写的月度新发现推荐。Molleson从作曲家传记的细致考据和新音乐节目的前沿声响两端出发，挑选了数张专辑进行介绍。内容涵盖解构式的tropicália实验、对一首四百年古老作品的清澈演绎，以及涉及演唱引用、加美兰等多种元素的当代音乐作品，其中包括Jessie Marino与Inga Margrete Aas及Pinquins的合作。整体选辑横跨当代古典、实验音乐与世界音乐传统，体现出对历史脉络与先锋探索并重的策展思路。原文内容相对简短，仅为专栏导言式介绍，缺少对各张专辑的具体深入评述。

items.body: In “Rokia”, a young villager falls in love with his neighbour, and her mother, Rokia, opposes the relationship. Rabie Houti, a violinist and singer from Oran in Algeria who has lived in Montpellier since 2014, tells the story with Gasba Électrique, who combine Maghrebi flute with electronic textures. The track brings together his Arabo-Andalusian violin, electronic beats and rock guitars, and builds gradually into a trance. Trance is the band’s own word for its live shows too, which have taken them from Montpellier to Canada, Algeria and Kazakhstan. Houti’s own road to those stages started in Oran, where his father loved Arabo-Andalusian music and his older sister Khedija taught him his first notes on a mandolin. Around the age of eight he played his first concert, on violin, with the junior orchestra of the Nassim El Andalous school at Oran’s opera house. These days he leads the Rabie Houti Band, active since 2017, who set Maghrebi melodies over funk and rock grooves and place themselves in “Sono Mondiale”, the movement the late Rachid Taha championed. Joudour, their second album, takes its title from the Arabic word for roots, and the band marked its release with a free show at Rockstore in Montpellier on 3 October. It follows Tahtaha from 2019, which Houti describes as a test from a time when the band was still searching; with Joudour, he says, they found their signature. The new album leans further into rock and electronics, and every track is an original composition. You can stream “Rokia” and Joudour HERE. The post Daily Discovery: Rabie Houti – Rokia appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: maghrebi fusion / arabic andalusian / electronic / world rock
items._cn_summary: 阿尔及利亚裔小提琴手兼歌手Rabie Houti现居蒙彼利埃，与乐队Gasba Électrique合作，将马格里布笛声与电子质感交织。作品以阿拉安德鲁西亚小提琴为核心，叠加电子节拍与摇滚吉他，层层递进进入恍惚状态。Houti自幼在奥兰歌剧院少年乐团习琴，后组建乐队活跃于蒙彼利埃、加拿大、阿尔及利亚及哈萨克斯坦等地舞台。新作标题Joudour在阿语中意为根源，整体倾向摇滚与电子融合，延续已故Rachid Taha倡导的Sono Mondiale运动路线，融合放克与摇滚律动承载马格里布旋律。所有曲目均为原创，第二张专辑在蒙彼利埃Rockstore以免费演出形式发布。

items.body: Her grandmother had run out of stories for the night. Go to the cow pen, she told six-year-old Kasiva Mutua , and listen to the secret the black bull is telling the white one. Kasiva went, listened, and returned having heard nothing but a bull sniffing the air. Her grandmother sent her back, told her to listen properly, that the secret was being told right now. The second time, she heard it. Crickets layered on top of each other. Cows breathing in something close to a shared tempo. Wind moving through the trees, laughter drifting from the kitchen. She started humming what she’d heard, then playing it out on her own bed frame, her lap, her chest and cheeks, and from there on anything within reach: pans, spoons, a school desk, a bucket. Percussion belonged to men in the community she grew up in. She took it up anyway, and kept at it until she was one of the only women in Kenya playing it at all, continentally or internationally, and eventually one of the best known. By 25 years old, she was a OneBeat Fellow, and the following year she joined The Nile Project, an East African touring collective she’s stayed with since. Two years later, in 2015, she co-founded MOTRAMUSIC in Nairobi, Kenya’s first all-female percussion collective, taking young women through a year of mentorship in rhythm, composition and performance. She’s also worked with Giant Steps Music and recorded for Coke Studio Africa. TED named her a Global Fellow in 2017, and she has spoken about the drum as a way of telling her own story. In 2020 a OneBeat Accelerator grant let her build Vibe na Queen, an online platform connecting Kenyan women musicians through the pandemic. Her 2022 debut EP Ngewa came after all of that, carrying what the teaching and the touring had put into her playing, and Desturi, her debut album released in February last year, picked up where it left off. Fifteen years, Kasiva says, is how long she has wanted to play WOMEX, hearing it talked about long before she ever stood near its stage, called the World Cup of performances by everyone who had been. On 23 October, in Las Palmas, it happens. She is bringing the album with her, and an open invitation: find her showcase, and come share it. She answered our questions for this year’s Musical Road to WOMEX, on the drum as a way of telling stories, on growing up in a place where it wasn’t meant to be hers, and on what she wants to find on the islands, and put together a playlist exclusively for Rhythm Passport, the tracks hers to choose.  You’ve described the drum as a way of telling your people’s stories. For someone hearing you for the first time, how would you introduce the sound you make now, and where does the voice sit alongside the percussion? Rhythm is a universal language. It’s also everywhere around us. It’s heard, felt, it brings movement (dance, nod, make faces of expression) and evokes emotions. There’s no one who is excluded from rhythm. Children, adults, animals, people of different abilities and backgrounds; we all understand and experience it. We carry rhythm within us throughout our lives, and when the rhythm stops, life ends. For someone hearing me for the first time, I’m a gentle reminder of the joy of having rhythm and how important it is to notice it. The way rhythm sounds and is expressed can vary depending on where we come from, our travels, experiences, and the people and environments we encounter. But in all those variations, is the same foundation; rhythm is something we all carry within us. My sound, then, is something familiar, rooted in East Africa and shaped by nature, my experiences, stories, and the many influences of our African cultures. You learned drumming from your grandmother in a community where the instrument was reserved for men. Looking back, what was the moment you understood that playing it would define your life rather than simply defy a rule? I was inspired by my grandmother’s stories that she told me that taught me to listen to nature. And that way, I started hearing sounds and eventually rhythm. I don’t think there’s an exact moment that stood out, rather a consistent chain of events that led me here. But I can remember a moment I asked myself “Surely, what else in the world can bring me this kind of joy? I LOVE this thing!” WOMEX lands this year in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, an Atlantic island with its own percussion: the tajaraste, driven by drum and chácaras, the big castanets thought to trace back to the islands’ North African roots. As a percussionist, what are you most curious to hear there? Eeeeeeeverything, man! I wanna hear everything! From the music, to how the children there laugh, and how the water hits the rocks. I’m very curious about the island’s stories too! In a WOMEX line-up full of the world’s traditions, what makes your showcase stand out, and what do you most want people to take from it? My best friend says that there’s nothing as beautiful as watching someone fully immersed in something they absolutely love. There’s something about witnessing that kind of joy; it makes you fall in love with them, and somehow, in the process, you fall in love with yourself all over again. Well… WOMEX is built on unexpected meetings. Are there particular artists, labels or collaborators you’re hoping to cross paths with in Las Palmas? Yes, I’m looking forward to the beautiful connections that will be born out of WOMEX. I’m particularly excited to meet female artists and instrumentalists, some who I have already connected on Instagram, and women working across the music industry. Your drumming is built to pull people in: call and response, bodies moving. A WOMEX audience is mostly music professionals, there to watch and assess rather than dance. How do you win a room like that? Yes, they may be music professionals, but before anything else, they’re human. They are someone’s son, somebody’s daughter. They have kids, They have feelings, emotions, relationships, memories, pain and joy. They’re an audience like any other. Rhythm doesn’t choose where to land or who it belongs to. Even I, myself, cannot control that. It simply does what it does. My role is to play and let it find its way to whoever is listening. Your travels have a way of turning up in your music. Ahead of your first time in the Canaries, is there anything about the islands, their rhythms, their sounds, you’re hoping to come away with? My travels have constantly shaped the person I am becoming. My interactions, experiences and stories all play a big part in the music to come. I’m very curious what this part of my musical journey will look like. In much of Africa the drum has been a man’s instrument, off-limits to women, and you are one of the few who took it up, made a life of it, and spent years bringing other women in behind you. Is there a message you feel especially compelled to carry to an international audience through this showcase? Ah yes. The beauty of our African cultures is that they are deeply complex and constantly evolving. I’ve lived through a time, before mobile phones and the internet, and now I’m living through this period of cultural transition, where we’re all negotiating what we carry forward and how it interacts with the world now. For a long time, the focus was on me being a woman holding a drum. But I think the focus needs to shift from who is playing the instrument to what is being played. I’ve dedicated my life to making sure the rhythms of my people continue to live and travel beyond home, to places where strangers can hear them, dance to them, and perhaps find something of themselves in them. It used to feel significant to be the only woman in the room holding a drum. Today, I’m less interested in that distinction. I’m more interested in the joy of sharing the music, traditions and stories that live within those rhythms, and allowing that to take centre stage. Having moved from percussion into songwriting, production and your own voice, what’s next? New recordings, new collaborations, a direction you haven’t tried yet? I’d prefer to see it as an “expansion of rhythm”. As I evolve, I am finding new ways of expression. I am very open to cultural evolution, and this brings in the aspect of collaboration. Traveling has deeply shaped who I’m becoming and interacting with different cultures adds to my musical DNA. Yes, there’s lots of music to come. Yes, there’s collaborations and yes, there’s many directions I haven’t tried and perhaps are unknown to me just yet. I’m also excited to discover this! If you could write a personal invitation to the people arriving in Las Palmas to come and find your showcase, what would it say? Let me tell you a little story… For about 15 years, as I backed many artists in Kenya and around the world, I always heard this name “WOMEX”. And how it was said to me meant “This is the ‘World Cup’ of performances!” I always wanted to play here. With anyone really. I just wanted to get on this stage. More than 15 years later, it’s going to happen! And with my Desturi, my debut album. WOMEX don’t really understand what they’ve done! They’ve allowed me to live a dream, and by doing so, have now given me permission to take on other dreams… My name is Kasiva Mutua. Find my showcase and come, share my dream come true with me on 23rd Oct, massive Friday night! I’d love to have you there! The bigger the party, the bigger the celebration! Yay! Ahsante! I love you!   Fifteen years of hearing WOMEX talked about end on a Friday night at Plaza del Espigón in Las Palmas. Kasiva Mutua plays there on 23 October, and she's already told the city what she wants from it: the bigger the party, the bigger the celebration!   PLAYLIST: KASIVA MUTUA X RHYTHM PASSPORT   You can find all the previous episodes of Musical Road to Womex HERE   The post Musical Road to WOMEX 2026 – Kasiva Mutua appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评围绕肯尼亚女性打击乐手Kasiva Mutua的音乐道路展开，介绍她从六岁时祖母引导她倾听自然中的节奏开始，逐步打破社区中打击乐属于男性的传统，成为肯尼亚乃至非洲大陆少数知名女性打击乐手之一。她曾入选OneBeat Fellows并加入The Nile Project巡回乐团，2015年在内罗毕联合创立肯尼亚首个全女性打击乐团体MOTRAMUSIC，提供节奏、作曲与表演的年度指导。她的首张EP《Ngewa》和专辑《Desturi》承载了多年演出与教学的积累，前者作为WOMEX 2026的展示项目在拉斯帕尔马斯呈现。Kasiva将鼓视为讲述自己民族故事的工具，强调节奏作为通用语言存在于自然、人声与身体律动之中。她的演奏融合了东非部落节奏与现代非洲融合语汇，作品面向世界音乐与世界节拍领域，体现出女性视角在传统打击乐中的独特表达。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — First it was FAIRPORT CONVENTION, but STEELEYE SPAN really planted the flag, and so were followed by worthy extenders in other lands, such as MALICORNE and TRI YANN in France, ANGELO BRANDUARDI and GIAN CASTELLO in Italy, CLANNAD and HORSLIPS in Ireland, MABSANT and PERERIN in Wales, CAPERCAILLIE and RUNRIG in Scotland, OUGENWEIDE and GALAHAD in Germany, MILLADOIRO and SANGRE DE MUERDAGO in Spain, and on and on. Most played a mix of trad/arranged and original/arranged trad style, such that, if you didn't already know, you'd be challenged to distinguish one from the other. They translated ancient poetry and prose into their native language and took liberties with the original melodies when they were known at all. I count myself among those who didn't realize that at least one Finnish group belongs in such select company, but given the breadth of Finnish prog folk, which is like THIS wide, I can't say I'm surprised by the presence or the quality of TARUJEN SAARI ("the island of sagas"), right from this debut.Led by the spirited and technically irreproachable vocals and woodwinds of Kaisa Saari, the hurdy gurdy and sundry from veteran TAPIO MATTLAR, twin violins, and a host of other folk instrumentation, this opening shot straddles all the aforementioned genealogical lines and draws a few of their own. When they choose a tune already well known to the type of people who would listen to this album in the first place, like "The Blacksmith", they give it a fresh spin, in this case it's more potent than the diva-ish LOREENA MCKENNITT rendition or the dirge like versions by STEELEYE SPAN when they were still finding themselves. They even tap the Swedes for the insistent "Margareeta". But the obvious standout here is Sinun Siniset silmasi" (your blue eyes), which merges flawless vocals, organic melody and guest cello.It's worth mentioning that for 30+ years a world beat group named VAARTINA has decorated their own room in trad oriented Finnish folk to an appreciative audience, but TARUJEN SAARI in unison pushes against the 4 (or however many) walls and thus, if not on the island of which they sing, can at least see it from their terrasse.

items._cn_summary: 这张芬兰前卫民谣专辑将传统乐器如手摇风琴、双小提琴与木管乐器结合，由Kaisa Saari主导的人声与器乐编排技术扎实。乐评将其置于欧洲各国民谣复兴的谱系中，与Fairport Convention、Steeleye Span、Malicorne等经典团体并列，强调他们对传统曲目的再诠释能力。专辑既包含对经典曲目如《The Blacksmith》的翻新处理，也融入瑞典民谣素材，整体展现芬兰传统民谣的多样性与文化深度。作为芬兰本土小众厂牌发行的处女作，其器乐配置丰富，但融合仍偏向传统民谣范畴内的扩展，与实验或前卫领域的交集有限。

items.body: I had hoped to be seen by you Unbroken gaze like a sweet arrow Could you ever feel my eyes on you Bathing you in my desire Desire has a way of making the body speak before the mind has decided what to say: flushed cheeks, an aching chest, the unreasonable hope that somebody might feel a glance from across the room. In the video for Sacred Hearts, Gloria de Oliveira takes those private sensations onto the streets of Hamburg’s St. Pauli district, where barroom lamps, photo-booth portraits, and the company of women give longing somewhere to live. The song’s burning heart finds a fitting companion in the red lights overhead, while affection passes between its subjects through looks, laughter, and the small pleasure of being together. The Berlin-based German-Brazilian musician and visual artist shares the video for the third single from her forthcoming album The Lying Swans, due October 30, 2026, through La Double Vie and Cargo Records. Produced by Randall Dunn, whose work includes records with Anna von Hausswolff and Marissa Nadler, Sacred Hearts considers the exhilaration and anxiety of giving yourself over to another person, particularly when the body seems to have made that decision ahead of you. The opening guitar figures carry an almost medieval character, joined by bright, percussive tones with the delicacy of a hammered dulcimer. Matt Chamberlain’s drumming briefly suggests the forward motion of Kate Bush’s Running Up That Hill before settling into the song’s own gait. Deep resonant strings lend the arrangement weight, while synthesizers soften its edges and extend its peculiar, old-world atmosphere. The tones and melody evoke a folk ballad like Nick Cave’s The Weeping Song, with the spaciousness of a Western just beyond the song’s antique ornamentation. De Oliveira sings into that space with a delicate quiver that evokes Elizabeth Fraser, with a classical poise softened by the intimacy of her delivery. Lennard Zander’s acoustic, electric, and 12-string guitars trace fine melodic lines without disturbing the vocal’s tenderness; Arjan Miranda anchors the arrangement on bass, while de Oliveira, Dunn, and Úlfur Hansson add layers of synthesizer. The music leaves her exposed yet almost weightless, as if every declaration of love might tip her toward losing her footing. The lyrics measure desire through its physical symptoms, moving from fever and sleeplessness toward the hope contained in a hand’s touch. To be seen becomes as urgent as to be loved, and the repeated attempts to contain that feeling only reveal its scale. Yet, the song’s title draws on an image de Oliveira has carried since childhood, joining religious devotion to the unruly sensations of romantic attachment. “The Catholic image of Christ’s Sacred Heart – a heart literally engulfed in flames – has struck me since childhood.” “Of course it’s meant to symbolise God’s boundless and passionate love for mankind – however, as John Keats once wrote, ‘I am certain of nothing but of the holiness of the heart’s affections, and the truth of imagination’. And how does it feel to give yourself over to that affection and desire despite fear? With this song, I wanted to capture these seemingly contrasting sentiments.” Shot and directed by award-winning Turkish filmmaker Seda Kaçak, and edited by de Oliveira, the video stars London actress Mona Najma alongside Eva Rogalla. Kaçak follows the women through St. Pauli in handheld close-ups, catching them sharing drinks, posing for photo-booth pictures, and moving between daylight streets and richly coloured interiors. Superimposed faces and starbursts around the lights give these ordinary pleasures an enchanted quality. Conceived as a homage to the bond between women, the film offers an affectionate counterpoint to the song’s solitary ache: companionship makes room for feelings that can otherwise become overwhelming. Watch the video for Sacred Hearts below: A classically trained singer whose acting work includes Babylon Berlin and Christian Petzold’s Undine, de Oliveira released music with the darkwave and synthpop duo lovespells before her 2020 debut album Fascination. Her 2022 collaboration with David Lynch’s longtime sound designer Dean Hurley, Oceans of Time, followed through Sacred Bones. Across those releases, she has explored dream pop, ethereal wave, ambient music, and the influence of her Brazilian roots, alongside work for theatre, film, and London Fashion Week. Recorded in Iceland, New York, and Berlin, The Lying Swans extends those interests across nine songs concerned with trauma, perception, and the difficult return of trust. Its title invokes the myth of Leda, while its literary references include John Keats, Emily Brontë, Anne Sexton, and Milton’s Paradise Lost. Within that broader examination of love and illusion, Sacred Hearts holds open the possibility of affection despite fear. Listen to Sacred Hearts below or via streaming services, and pre-order The Lying Swans here. The album is out October 30, 2026, on digital, vinyl, CD, and cassette. items.body: …O sun, that healest all distempered vision, thou dost content me so, when thou resolvest,that doubting pleases me no less than knowing! -Dante Alighieri, Divine Comedy Golden Apes have spent more than twenty years making music for people who think a bass guitar should sound slightly dangerous, a baritone ought to carry bad news with dignity, and every decent chorus deserves at least one guitar line large enough to knock over the furniture. On The Sun Came Up Tremendously, the Berlin band sounds completely at home with that assignment. Ten songs move between post-punk, dark wave, gothic rock, dreampop, and bruised alternative rock, yet the record never feels like a display cabinet of influences. Golden Apes know this country too well for tourism. They have lived here. There is plenty of history in these songs, of course. You can hear The Cure in the open space around certain guitar lines, Chameleons in the upward sweep of others, Cocteau Twins in the gauzier passages, and the severe romantic machinery of Clan of Xymox when the keyboards begin closing in. White Lies, Interpol, Lowlife, and The Horrors, drift through the bloodline. Yet Golden Apes have reached the point where influence is less a matter of borrowing than instinct. Twenty-plus years will do that to a band. Eventually your record collection gets absorbed into your nervous system. The Sun Came Up Tremendously follows 2024’s Our Ashes at the End of the Day as the second installment in a planned trilogy, with material written across 2024 and 2025 and recorded at Thommy Hein Studios in Berlin between late 2025 and early 2026. Thommy Hein also contributes guitar, joining vocalist and keyboardist Peer Lebrecht, guitarists Maximilian Hennig and Stephan Schoenfeld, bassist Christian Lebrecht, and drummer Salomon Bosse. The production favors size without polishing away the pressure inside these songs. Basslines keep pushing forward, drums give the record a stern physical gait, and the guitars are allowed to bloom, bruise, and occasionally swallow the room. Farewell begins with a plaintive guitar that sounds as if it’s emerging from a dream, and an open space that immediately calls The Chameleons to mind, though The Horrors’ later grandeur also shows in the way the arrangement keeps adding height. It is a lovely opening, sad without collapsing into self-pity, and expansive without turning into marble-statue rock. Peer Lebrecht sings as though he has already accepted whatever the song is grieving, which somehow makes the ache sharper. By the time the rhythm section settles in, the track feels less like a goodbye than the long walk away from one. The Light (Inside Us) comes on harder. The guitars widen, Christian Lebrecht’s bass digs in, and the verses carry a conversational quality before the chorus breaks open into a shoegaze-heavy rush. The seduction of scale takes center stage: the chorus is huge enough to make a ceiling seem temporarily optional, yet the band keeps enough dirt in the guitars to prevent grandeur from becoming ceremony. This is music reaching for the upper rows while keeping both boots on the club floor. Milk and Poison turns inward and drops the temperature. Its opening feels like ripples on water with dream-pop textures, though the song soon settles into an anthemic ballad buoyed by these currents, sailing on broad synth pads, acoustic accents, surging guitars, and Peer’s low, expressive voice. He has one of those voices that can make a grocery list sound vaguely incriminating, and Golden Apes wisely avoid burying it beneath unnecessary decoration. The arrangement gives him room, then closes around him in slow degrees. Resistance is where the record’s architecture comes into sharpest focus. A resonant guitar figure opens the track, answered by a low keyboard tone, as hi-hats hiss at the edges and the bass builds steady pressure. The arrangement grows heavier until the guitars reach the emotional scale of mid-eighties gothic rock. Peer remains composed as the band swells around him, and that restraint gives the song its authority. Near the center, a clean, melodic guitar solo arrives with almost startling simplicity, offering a brief clearing before the vocal returns with greater weight. No pyrotechnics are needed; the song already knows where its gravity lies. At intervals, the drums break into splashes and the rhythm pulls back, leaving more air around Peer’s euphoric delivery. The measured bass, sober guitar tone, and baritone gravity recall Scottish cult band Lowlife, while the surrounding textures remain recognizably Golden Apes. Helion heads toward the same terrain as Clan of Xymox and The Chameleons, with traces of Joy Division in its resigned vocals and the stern drive of its rhythm section. An emotional barrage of drums and surging guitars carries the song forward, giving its sense of exhaustion an almost overwhelming physical force. There is something perversely satisfying about how controlled it remains amid all that turbulence. Plenty of bands mistake gloom for permission to wallow; Golden Apes keep pushing through it. It is the sort of song you want to hear live, feel in your chest, and carry with you on the walk home after everybody else has disappeared. Where the River Ran slows the pace and brings Peer’s baritone into Nick Cave territory. The drums begin with a plodding military tattoo, giving the song a processional character, while guitar and synth gradually stretch outward until the arrangement takes on a shoegaze breadth. The transition works because the band allows it to happen patiently. What begins in discipline ends in something far less contained. Evelyn (One Day) opens with a long sigh, which is about as efficient a piece of scene-setting as anybody could ask for. The resemblance to Lowlife grows even stronger here, recalling the Scottish band at their most wistful, thoughtful, and romantic. Dream-pop synth textures surround Peer’s voice, while dramatic splashes of guitar and percussion accent the song’s tender emotion, not unlike The Cure’s “Push.” Once again, Golden Apes take the form of a ballad and keep expanding it until the walls seem to move outward. The song swells like the ocean, its quieter passages gathering strength before euphoric surges of guitar and drums break across the arrangement. Their fondness for large choruses could become ridiculous in less experienced hands, but the rhythm section keeps the drama tethered to muscle. Radiation opens with a steady drumbeat and dirgeful tones before Peer’s rich, deep baritone bellows with unusual force, almost thunderous without losing definition. The chiming guitars and rhythm section pull back to give him room, though the melodic bassline remains palpable, felt in the heart and bones. With the song’s titular refrain, a surge of guitars seems to radiate toward the fingertips, giving its emotional release a physical reach. The drums then quicken in anticipation, and the guitars sweep in sustained arcs before the refrain returns, each repetition gathering strength from the space the band leaves around the voice. City Walls slows everything again, returning to the Cave-like gravity heard earlier. The drums drag with deliberate weight while a manic hi-hat keeps scratching at the surface, and eerie female backing vocals add an uneasy human presence around Peer’s lead. The song feels boxed in by design. Space exists, but none of it seems comfortable. Every instrument appears to occupy its own corner while the room keeps shrinking. Then comes Dreams (Gone By), opening with strange industrial textures before a weighty rhythm section and eerie synth tones take control, recalling London After Midnight’s Kiss. The percussion has real physical heft, but the gloom gradually recedes as the song opens into the brighter dream-pop romance of Modern English and Lowlife. Golden Apes carry that change with the emotional swell established throughout the album, letting the arrangement expand without losing the force of its darker beginnings. A brief pause for a wistful guitar chime offers some breathing room before the gothic dance rhythm returns, subtly brighter now, and the song surges again. As a closer, it gives the album one last change in texture, moving from industrial unease toward romantic release while retaining the emotional weight of the previous nine tracks. By this point, the record has passed through goth, post-punk, dreampop, dark wave, and broad alternative rock without sounding indecisive. Golden Apes can write a severe club track, a huge guitar chorus, a graveyard ballad, or a slow piece that sounds built for stained glass and bad decisions, and somehow Peer Lebrecht’s voice keeps the record unified. His baritone carries longing, isolation, regret, and the occasional flash of release without turning every lyric into a public execution. There is drama here, plenty of it, but the band understands proportion. Even at their biggest, they leave enough space for the songs to breathe. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is also the work of a band with very little interest in pretending they discovered any of these styles yesterday. Golden Apes’ long touring history, including appearances at Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Castle Party, and Murder of Crows, plus stages shared with The Chameleons, Pink Turns Blue, And Also the Trees, She Past Away, Whispering Sons, TRAITRS, Then Comes Silence, and others, has given them the practical education that comes from watching songs survive outside the studio. The title may promise sunrise, though nobody should expect birds chirping outside a kitchen window. Golden Apes prefer their light complicated, filtered through regret, desire, bad choices, and the stubborn suspicion that survival can occasionally be worth the inconvenience of a journey through hell and back. The only way to reach dawn, after all, is through the night. The Sun Came Up Tremendously is out now through Icy Cold Records. Listen to the album below and order here. items._cn_summary: Golden Apes是来自柏林的后朋克乐队，组建逾二十年，2026年发行专辑《The Sun Came Up Tremendously》，为计划三部曲的第二部。专辑横跨后朋克、暗潮、哥特摇滚、梦幻流行与shoegaze等多种风格，但听感连贯统一。评论将乐队声音谱系追溯至The Cure、Chameleons、Cocteau Twins、Clan of Xymox、White Lies、Interpol等乐队的影响，但强调Golden Apes已将前辈语言内化为自身本能。制作上追求宏大规模而不失内在压力感，贝斯线持续推进，鼓点沉稳，吉他层叠开放时而吞没空间。主唱Peer Lebrecht的声线沉郁而庄重，开篇曲《Farewell》以梦境般的吉他引入，悲伤却不自溺；《The Light (Inside Us)》则更为激烈，副歌在shoegaze音墙中炸裂开来。整体而言，这是一支成熟乐队对自身传统语汇的扎实延续。

items.body: Label: Out Of Your Head Records, 2026 Personnel - David Léon: saxophone, flute; Kenny Warren: trumpet; Stephan Crump: bass; Ches Smith: drums. Bassist and composer Stephan Crump, a musician of extraordinary passion and lyricism, put together a crisp, bright new ensemble for his latest outing, Passerine , a work of originals inspired by the various nesting techniques of birds. Relying on a frontline composed of Cuban-American saxophonist and flutist David Léon and trumpeter Kenny Warren, and pairing up beautifully with the resourceful drummer Ches Smith, Crump has something fresh to say. " Stuck " firstly evolves in a 3/4 time signature, displaying a big, round bass sound that shelters sharp unison melody. Léon narrates a story over an arco bass ostinato, while Smith explores toms and cymbal sounds with sagacity. There's a change of pace and texture for Warren's expressive solo, and the interplay between the rhythm team becomes more defiant, leading to a swinging passage before returning to the initial waltzing breeze. " Glide " is executed with a compelling rhythmic quality underneath—Crump incorporating effortless bass pedals, pizzicato routes, and cool grooves that find consistent support in Smith's nicely brushed skins. On flute, Léon stands out, drawing from melodic and harmonic minor modes in his improvisation. " Weavers " and " Twenty-Five " are warm meditative exercises where all members leave flowery scents in the air while rowing in the same direction. The former piece rests on a relaxed bass harmonic conduction that breathes at a challenging tempo, having charismatic, pure-toned unisons running atop. The latter is a shape-shifter that initiates with a sparse bass figure, understated drumming, a pellucid flute whose gentle dance emulates the chirp of birds, and introspective trumpet. Warren and Léon always take maximum advantage of their instruments to create dual melodic lines that feel luminous and often varied in shape. That's the case on " Fly ", a well-balanced 3/4 canvas painted with a certain wry melancholia. Breathable bass and brush work create space and smooth out the environment, culminating in a pulsating bass pedal point at the center of the outro vamp. With sensitive collaborative input from the musicians enlisted, Passerine is a point of departure and an embrace of transformation for Crump. It's also detailed with rigor without abandoning the freedom of creating spontaneously. The composer's sophisticated sound and gracious storytelling are filtered into the album's sequence. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Stuck ► 02 - Glide ► 03 - Weavers

items._cn_summary: 贝斯手兼作曲家 Stephan Crump 以鸟类筑巢方式为灵感，创作了这张以原创曲目为主的现代爵士作品。编制为萨克斯/长笛、小号、贝斯与鼓的典型四重配置，整体气质偏向学院派即兴与室内爵士的交叉地带。乐评着重描述了各曲目的节奏结构与乐器互动：3/4 拍与摇摆段落交替，弓弦拨弦与低音踏板构成多层次的贝斯线条，长笛与小号形成双重旋律线，既有温暖冥想段落也有诙谐忧郁的铺陈。文本中虽提及自由即兴与互动，但整体仍属框架内的现代爵士创作，独立厂牌发行，篇幅充足，是一篇信息密度较高的原创乐评。

items.body: Watch an exclusive premiere of the film of Ava Rasti’s The River, first performed as part of the 2025 Semibreve festival. The River by Iranian-born Berlin-based composer Ava Rasti was commissioned by Portuguese festival Semibreve and first presented on 25 October 2025 at the Capela Imaculada do Seminário Menor in Braga. The performance brought together Rasti and a string quartet composed of Filipa Abreu (violin), Vânia Oliveira (viola), Tiago Mendes (cello) and Catarina Coelho (cello). The work takes the Piave river in northern Italy as its inspiration, a landscape in which the present is intertwined with the traces of wars and violence from its past. Rasti constructs these fragmented memories, recontextualised and transformed into sounds. Wire subscribers can read Claire Sawer's review of Semibreve 2025 here.

items._cn_summary: 伊朗裔柏林作曲家Ava Rasti受葡萄牙Semibreve音乐节委约，创作了弦乐四重奏与现场影像作品《The River》。作品以意大利北部皮亚韦河为灵感来源，这条河流沿岸曾经历战争创伤，地景中至今保留着暴力的历史痕迹。Rasti将这些碎片化的记忆重新编排并转化为声响，通过弦乐四重奏的演奏（两位小提琴、一位中提琴、两位大提琴）构建出具有实验性的当代古典音乐文本。作品首演于2025年10月25日在布拉加的教堂空间中举行。整体属于当代古典与现代作曲范畴，结合了场地特定的委约创作模式与历史记忆的声音化处理，具有一定的实验性和文化叙事深度。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — Truly mind blowing album. Arguably one of the most manifold records from the dusk of that decade. HIGH TIDE have been one of the most important underground rock acts of that era. This album really blew my mind the first time I heard it. I almost did not believe that it released in 1969. Very few bands were so heavy back then. HIGH TIDE is so damn heavy, it really pisses me off that I can't recall a single magazine or online "list" of proto-metal bands that mentions these guys. You can find fragments of early doom in songs like "Futilist's lament" & "Missing out". You can hear neoclassical influences on the guitar riff on "Walking down their outlook". Also, on the same song, listen carefully the guitar lick on 2:20 (Judas Priest anyone?!?!?). And that violin... Majestic. Enchanting. Listen to "Pushed, but not forgotten". Amazing stuff, honestly. Some people may say that the [&*!#]ty production fits with the music and the atmosphere, I say it steals the music's grandeur.

items._cn_summary: High Tide 1969年首张专辑以沉重厚重的吉他音色和小提琴的运用在同时代极为罕见，评论者将其定位为proto-metal的先驱之一。专辑融合了新古典主义影响的吉他riff、早期doom的碎片化段落以及迷幻氛围，小提琴作为主导乐器为整体增添了庄严而迷幻的质感。曲目如《Futilist's Lament》《Missing Out》展现了末日感的沉重段落，而《Walking Down Their Outlook》中的吉他lick被指与后来Judas Priest的风格遥相呼应。评论者认为专辑制作粗糙，削弱了音乐的宏大感，但音乐本身的实验性和前卫气质使其成为地下摇滚史上的重要作品。整体偏向英伦地下摇滚场景，带有早期前卫金属和迷幻摇滚的混合特征。

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — One of my favorite albums of 1969 hands down. So many styles of music one can find here. Blues, psychedelia, jazz, classical, rock. All of them combined to provide a sample of proto-prog in the late 60s British scene. Songs like "Isadora", "Waterways", "Bathers", "Moth" are majestic. Geoff Nicholson delivers some really beautiful and heart-warming vocal harmonies. But, Dave Arbus steals the show here. With his electric violin and his flute, he blesses our ears with some enchanting melodies. This album really could be close to perfect, if it weren't for those free jazz/improvisations on the songs "Centaur woman" & "In the stable of the Sphinx" which in my opinion kind of mess up a little bit the whole atmosphere of the album.Nevertheless, this is a really strong album, that the fans of the early prog rock era should check out.
items._genre: eclectic prog / psych rock / jazz fusion
items._cn_summary: 1969年英国乐队East of Eden的专辑融合了布鲁斯、迷幻摇滚、爵士与古典元素，是前卫摇滚萌芽阶段的代表作品。Geoff Nicholson的人声和声温暖饱满，而Dave Arbus的小提琴与长笛演奏成为专辑亮点，呈现出灵动而丰富的器乐层次。然而评论者指出，Centaur Woman与In the Stable of the Sphinx中的自由即兴段落破坏了整体氛围的统一性，使专辑未能达到完美水准。整体而言，这是一张风格跨度宽泛、充满实验精神的早期前卫摇滚作品，对60年代末英国音乐场景具有重要参考价值，适合关注摇滚乐历史与早期前卫音乐融合的听众。

items.body: Colossloth released a video for “Encoded Divinity” on 3 October 2026, a track from the album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites.” The album came out 2 October 2026 on Cold Spring Records, the project’s sixth release for the label. The video was produced by HAONDOKU Productions. The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites by Colossloth Watch the video for ‘Encoded Divinity’ The video is available on YouTube: COLOSSLOTH – ‘Encoded Divinity’ Promo Video. “Encoded Divinity” opens the album and runs 5:08. ‘The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites’ tracklist The album was announced in September with its full tracklist: “Encoded Divinity” (5:08) “Calculate Your Revolution” (7:00) “Awaiting MENA” (9:04) “Undertow Atlas” (10:34) “Only Adrift” (8:00) Cold Spring describes the album as centered on Theta Noir, a collective built around worship of Mena, a fictional artificial intelligence deity. The label calls the record “an automaton chant of cybernetic worship.” The album is available on CD in a matt-laminate digipak (catalogue number CSR375CD) through Cold Spring’s webstore, and for download via Bandcamp. Colossloth played an album launch show at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, alongside T.A.G.C. (Adi Newton of Clock DVA), Satøri and Llyn Y Cwn. Further dates follow on 7 November at St Anne’s in Barnstaple with Satøri and A Waste of Damnation, and from 27 to 29 November at Sheffield General Cemetery’s In The Black Midwinter event with The Golden Age of Doing Nothing and Decommissioned Forests. About Colossloth Colossloth is the solo project of Leicester, UK musician Wooly Woolaston, active since 2008. Woolaston has described Colossloth as “a one man Experimental Electronic artist where there are no rules to recording or playing music,” with a sound that has moved from long guitar drones toward harsher electronics with sections of melody. Woolaston released Colossloth’s first album through Doom Structure in 2008, followed by releases on Doom Mantra Records in 2009 and Dark Meadow Recordings in 2011. He later signed to Cold Spring Records, releasing “Anchored By Lungs” (2014), “Outstretch Your Hand for the Impress of Truth” (2015), “Heathen Needles” (2017), “Plague Alone” (2020) and “Promethean Meat” (2022), the latter incorporating drum samples and harsher rhythmic elements. Colossloth also appeared on the label’s “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” compilation alongside Coil, Merzbow and Mz.412, among others. Colossloth’s fifth Cold Spring album, “The Harmony Knife,” followed on 28 February 2025, a concept record drawing on Ted Kaczynski’s “Industrial Society and Its Future” and its argument for the psychological necessity of struggle, known as “the power process.” “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites,” released 2 October 2026, is Colossloth’s sixth album for Cold Spring Records, now accompanied by a video for its opening track, “Encoded Divinity.”

items._cn_summary: Colossloth 是一位来自英国莱斯特的实验电子音乐人，2026年10月发行第六张Cold Spring厂牌专辑《The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites》。专辑围绕虚构人工智能崇拜主题展开，厂牌将其描述为机械诵经式的赛博崇拜声响。音乐风格从早期长篇吉他drone逐渐转向更硬朗的电子声响，融入了鼓采样与节奏元素。曲目时长从五到十分钟不等，呈现典型的暗潮/工业实验电子特征。专辑以CD digipak形式发行，并在Glossop等地举办现场演出。整体定位属于地下实验电子领域，融合暗潮氛围与工业噪音美学，但未展现出突破性的声音创新，更多延续了既有风格脉络。

items.body: Einstürzende Neubauten’s debut studio album, “Kollaps,” turns 45 this year. The German industrial band released the record on 5 October 1981 through the Hamburg label ZickZack. It remains the first official full-length release by Blixa Bargeld, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit under the Einstürzende Neubauten name. “Kollaps” runs 38 minutes across eleven tracks, recorded in Berlin in 1981 and produced by the band itself. The album mixes rough punk-derived song structures with noise generated from self-built devices, electronics and metal plates and other found objects, a method that became the band’s signature. The tracklist includes “Tanz Debil,” “Steh auf Berlin,” “Negativ Nein,” “U-Haft Muzak,” “Draußen ist Feindlich,” “Schmerzen Hören (Hören mit Schmerzen),” “Jet’M” (a cover of Serge Gainsbourg’s “Je t’aime… moi non plus”), the title track “Kollaps,” “Sehnsucht,” “Vorm Krieg” and “Hirnsäge.” Later CD reissues appended additional tracks, including a live 1987 recording of “Negativ Nein.” Trouser Press described the record as “one of the most shocking visions ever committed to vinyl.” “Kollaps” is also listed in the reference book “1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.” The album has since been reissued, including a 2002 edition paired with the 1982 dub companion “Stahldubversions.” About Einstürzende Neubauten Einstürzende Neubauten formed in Berlin in 1980 around vocalist and guitarist Blixa Bargeld and percussionist N.U. Unruh. The band’s name translates to “collapsing new buildings,” a reference to construction failures in West Berlin at the time. From the outset, the group built its sound around self-made and adapted instruments, including power tools, scrap metal, oil drums and construction debris, played alongside conventional guitar, bass and vocals. F.M. Einheit joined on percussion before the band’s first LP. The band’s earliest recorded appearance came via the cassette-only “Stahlmusik” in 1980. Einstürzende Neubauten signed to the Hamburg independent label ZickZack, which released “Kollaps” on 5 October 1981, the band’s first official studio album. The record was recorded in Berlin during 1981 and produced by the band itself, with no outside producer credited. Following “Kollaps,” Einstürzende Neubauten continued to record for European independent labels through the 1980s, including “Zeichnungen des Patienten O.T.” (1983) and the compilation “Strategies Against Architecture ’80-’83,” before moving to Some Bizzare/Mute for later releases. Bargeld also worked as a guitarist with Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds from the band’s formation in 1983. Einstürzende Neubauten’s lineup has changed over four decades, with Alexander Hacke and Marc Chung both joining in the years following “Kollaps.” The band added bassist Josefine Lukschy in 2026, alongside confirmed festival dates and studio webcasts. Forty-five years after “Kollaps” introduced the band’s self-made-instrument method on record, Einstürzende Neubauten remains active, with the album standing as the starting point of that catalogue.
items._genre: industrial / experimental / post-punk / noise
items._cn_summary: 这篇报道介绍了Einstürzende Neubauten 1981年的首张录音室专辑《Kollaps》即将迎来45周年。专辑收录十一首曲目，录制于柏林，由乐队自行制作，时长约38分钟。其核心特征在于将粗糙的朋克结构与自製装置、电子设备、金属板及拾得物产生的噪音融为一体，开创性地利用电钻、油桶、建筑废料等作为打击声源，模糊了音乐与工业噪音的界限。曲目包括《Tanz Debil》《Steh auf Berlin》及翻唱自Serge Gainsbourg的《Jet'M》等。专辑被Trouser Press形容为"刻录于黑胶之上最具冲击力的幻象之一"，亦入选《1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die》。2002年再版时与1982年dub混音专辑《Stahldubversions》合辑发行。乐队成员Blixa Bargeld此后亦担任Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds吉他手。

items.excerpt: 会期：2026/08/05 会場：京都芸術センター 講堂［京都府］ 公式サイト： https://www.kac.or.jp/events/260805/ （前編より） すでに見たように、本作『ジェローム・ベル』の構造の肝は、メタ・ダンスである自作についてのレクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、さらにそれ自体が何重にもねじれたメタ・ダンス性をもつ点にある。パリ・オペラ座バレエ団のバレリーナやマース・カニングハム舞踊団のダンサー、タイ古典舞踊のダンサーなど、「多様なバックグラウンドをもつダンサーが自身について語るドキュメンタリー作品」を制作してきた振付家が、自分自身にそのメソッドを適用しつつ、「本人ではない他者に自伝を語らせる」というねじれや矛盾。ベル自身は、気候変動対策がきっかけであったと述べるが、ここでは、ダンス（舞台芸術）が反復性・再現可能性を前提とすることそれ自体が俎上に乗せられている。 冒頭、舞台に登場した川口隆夫は、前説を述べ、机に座ってノートパソコンを開けると、「私はジェローム・ベルです」とおもむろに自己紹介を始める。「16歳の娘がいます」「今57歳です」「振付家です」。川口自
items.body: 会期：2026/08/05 会場：京都芸術センター 講堂［京都府］ 公式サイト： https://www.kac.or.jp/events/260805/ （前編より） すでに見たように、本作『ジェローム・ベル』の構造の肝は、メタ・ダンスである自作についてのレクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、さらにそれ自体が何重にもねじれたメタ・ダンス性をもつ点にある。パリ・オペラ座バレエ団のバレリーナやマース・カニングハム舞踊団のダンサー、タイ古典舞踊のダンサーなど、「多様なバックグラウンドをもつダンサーが自身について語るドキュメンタリー作品」を制作してきた振付家が、自分自身にそのメソッドを適用しつつ、「本人ではない他者に自伝を語らせる」というねじれや矛盾。ベル自身は、気候変動対策がきっかけであったと述べるが、ここでは、ダンス（舞台芸術）が反復性・再現可能性を前提とすることそれ自体が俎上に乗せられている。 冒頭、舞台に登場した川口隆夫は、前説を述べ、机に座ってノートパソコンを開けると、「私はジェローム・ベルです」とおもむろに自己紹介を始める。「16歳の娘がいます」「今57歳です」「振付家です」。川口自身も振付家としてダンス作品を創作しており（そのなかには、記録映像に基づいて大野一雄の舞踏を完コピする『大野一雄について』［2013］というメタ・ダンス的作品も含まれる）、年齢も近いが、川口は俳優のようにベルを演じているわけではなく、書かれたテキストを日本語で読み上げ、指定された箇所でパソコンを操作して映像を再生させている。舞台上で語られるのは、ダンスをめぐる自作の思索に加え、ダンスとの出会い、エイズによる親友の死、父親になった喜びなどの自伝的語りだが、ベル自身は舞台上には一切姿を現わさず、指定した台詞を他者にしゃべらせ、パソコンを操作させている。ここで顕現するのは、「他者の身体を遠隔操作する」というまさに振付の力学だ。観客は、振付家としてのベル自身についての語りを聞きながら、同時に「他者の身体に及ぼされている振付の作用」そのものを目撃する。 ［Documentation Team © 2026 Hot Summer in Kyoto］ ベル自身、常に「振付（家）という権力性」についてラディカルかつ自己言及的に問うてきたが、本作のタイトル『ジェローム・ベル』は、作品名であると同時に振付家としての署名・・でもある。言い換えれば、この作品は『川口隆夫』ではない。出演者が「その人自身であること」は限りなく希薄化し、消去される。本作は、振付家としての成功も失敗も赤裸々に語られ、失恋や子どもの成長を見守る喜びなど私的な側面も率直に語る、一見誠実なドキュメンタリーでありつつ、完全に非ドキュメンタリーでもある。ここには、「ドキュメンタリー・シアターははたしてどこまで成立可能なのか？」という矛盾した問いも内包されている。一方、本作では、ベル／川口の境界線がわずかに揺らぐ瞬間もある。90年代初めにエイズで友人を亡くしたことが語られるシーンでは、「ダムタイプ」に参加した経歴をもつ川口が、自身の過去を重ね合わせているような沈黙の間があった。 本作はまた、舞台作品の基盤にある反復性や代演可能性を問うとともに、映像アーカイブと舞台芸術の一回性をめぐる問題も内包する。作中では、ダンス作品がスペクタクルな消費社会の速度に抗う抵抗として、繰り返し「今、ここ」にいることの重要性が説かれる。一方、作中で抜粋映像が紹介される自作について、「全編はYoutubeで見れます」と何度も述べられる。「自作についての解説が、それ自体を裏切り、新たな問いを派生させる」という構造がここにもある。 レクチャー・パフォーマンスであり、多層的なメタ・ダンス作品であり、「ドキュメンタリー」の成立（不）可能性をめぐる問いであり、映像アーカイブと舞台のライブ性に対する問いでもある本作。最後に、「クレジット」にも施された仕掛けについて触れたい。「出演」は、川口隆夫だけではなく、「記録映像」で紹介された過去の自作に出演した人物の名前がすべて列挙され、長大なリストをなしている。ここには、「作品の出演者」とは誰を指すのか？ という問いかけとともに、「過去作品に出演した 彼ら全員・・・・とともにこの作品がある」という敬意と誠意が込められている。 鑑賞日：2026/08/05（水） 関連レビュー 未だ見ぬ身体へ──川口隆夫『大野一雄について』｜岡村恵子：フォーカス（2017年11月15日号） 川口隆夫ソロダンスパフォーマンス『大野一雄について』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2015年12月15日号）

items._cn_summary: 本乐评围绕京都艺术中心上演的『ジェローム・ベル』展开，这是一部由振付家杰罗姆·贝尔创作、川口隆夫演绎的舞蹈公演。作品核心是一种多层嵌套的元舞蹈结构：川口在舞台上朗读贝尔的文本，操作笔记本电脑播放影像，以「他者」身份代替本尊完成自传式讲述，使「他人身体被远程操控」的编舞力学本身得以显形。乐评详细剖析了作品中的身份边界、文献记录与舞台现场的反差，以及编舞的权力性问题；同时通过川口曾参与ダムタイプ的经历与贝尔因艾滋病失去挚友的叙述交叠，揭示出演者与角色之间微妙模糊的瞬间。结尾的「出演」名单中列入所有过往作品参与者，体现对艺术劳动的敬意与作品代演可能性的反思。

items.excerpt: Label: Northern Spy Records, 2026 Personnel - Jeremy Cunningham: drumset, percussion, piano, Rhodes, organ, vibes, electronics; Jeff Parker: guitar; Josh Johnson: alto saxophone, electronics; Dustin Laurenzi: guitar, synth, programming, tenor saxophone; Matt Gold: guitar, bass, pandeiro; Greg Uhlmann; guitar, electronics; Will Miller: Rhodes, electronics; Sen Morimoto: vocals; Lia Kohl; cello; Paul Bryan: bass, electronics; Lane Beckstrom: bass; Makaya McCraven: drumset, vibes. Jeremy Cunningham
items.body: Label: Northern Spy Records, 2026 Personnel - Jeremy Cunningham: drumset, percussion, piano, Rhodes, organ, vibes, electronics; Jeff Parker: guitar; Josh Johnson: alto saxophone, electronics; Dustin Laurenzi: guitar, synth, programming, tenor saxophone; Matt Gold: guitar, bass, pandeiro; Greg Uhlmann; guitar, electronics; Will Miller: Rhodes, electronics; Sen Morimoto: vocals; Lia Kohl; cello; Paul Bryan: bass, electronics; Lane Beckstrom: bass; Makaya McCraven: drumset, vibes. Jeremy Cunningham is an alert and versatile multi-instrumentalist based in Chicago since 2009. I was very well impressed with his previous outing, A Better Ghost (2022), featuring a few members who reappear on Passing Fires , namely saxophonists Dustin Laurenzi and Josh Johnson, bassist Paul Bryan, and trumpeter-turned-keyboardist Will Miller. Other illustrious guests here include guitarists Jeff Parker and Matt Gold, and sophisticated drummer Makaya McCraven. Instead of fixed formats, Cunningham favors a rotation of musicians who have an ear for careful sonic detail. The album has a very personal feel to it, evolving as a meditation on love, loss, memory, and change. Two of the strongest pieces are " To The Sky " and " Kobi Shobi ". While the former holds a wonderful collective bossa groove, featuring the multi-faceted Matt Gold on guitar, bass, and pandeiro, Cunningham on Rhodes, McCraven's soulful drumming, and Japanese-American Sen Morimoto's ethereal, wordless vocal work, the latter is unexpectedly edgy, bolstered by funk throbs and a jazzy hip-hop vibe that takes us to A Tribe Called Quest and Digable Planets. Johnson's snaky alto solo boosts the energy over the syncopated guitar comping offered by Parker. Also filled with joy and aplomb, " Union Pier " is a compelling 3/4 duo piece that pairs Cunningham on drum set and percussion with Laurenzi, who, besides tenor—on which he offers a fluid improvisation—also injects guitar, synth, and percussion. " Beyond the Veil " is a 4/4 pop/rock piece with rounded harmonic contours and a graceful melody, featuring McCraven on vibes, and Parker, who claims the spotlight while injecting deep feeling into his impromptu statement. He also appears on the pop-meets-R&B " Some Days ”. Bryan's six-beat funky groove stretches into asymmetry and a different figure on " Galloway Street ", which welcomes guitarist Greg Uhlmann and shines a spotlight on Johnson's effect-drenched alto solo. The album closes in a Sade-like sophisti-pop style with " Somewhere To Be ", featuring Morimoto's smooth styling. Cunningham's compositions have a strong emotional arc, and that quality rings true in the music. Melding jazz-imbued improvisation into different stylistic frameworks, Passing Fires works as an escape from traditional jazz moves. Favorite Tracks: 03 - To The Sky ► 06 - Kobi Shobi ► 10 - Galloway Street

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由芝加哥多乐器演奏家Jeremy Cunningham领衔，邀请了Jeff Parker、Josh Johnson、Matt Gold、Makaya McCraven等十余位乐手参与，没有固定编制，而是根据作品需要轮换搭配。Cunningham本人演奏鼓、打击乐、钢琴、Rhodes、键盘、颤音琴及电子设备，横跨多种音色。专辑围绕爱、失去、记忆与变迁展开，风格跨度极大：bossa律动、funk hip-hop、3/4拍即兴、流行摇滚、Sade式sophisti-pop等不同框架并存。Josh Johnson的alto sax独奏贯穿多首作品，与Parker的吉他comping形成蛇形对话；Cunningham的作曲带有强烈的情感弧线，将爵士即兴融入不同风格结构中，试图逃离传统爵士套路。Northern Spy是小众独立厂牌，音乐上虽以爵士为骨架但大量融合电子与世界元素，偏向跨界实验路线。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.
Find out more about Merodefestival.

(Interview)

Songbooks Live

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了十三支比利时创新乐团的作品，录制于鲁汶附近的帕克修道院，利用古建筑天然混响营造冥想氛围。音乐横跨罗马吉普赛传统、手风琴为主的法式巴尔舞、地中海与阿拉伯融合、巴洛克风格的曼陀林与羽管键琴组合，以及带有中世纪意象的单簧管独奏。专辑在多元风格中保持内在统一性，乐手从修道院的壁画与空间汲取灵感，将比利时本土与世界音乐元素编织成层次丰富的器乐作品。录音由Bert Huysentruyt完成，Pieter De Wagter负责母带处理，三年制作周期。整体偏向氛围化与跨界融合，但实验性与前卫程度有限，更接近精致的世界音乐合辑。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以乌克兰传统民歌为底色，围绕俄方占领后约两万乌克兰儿童被强制带往俄罗斯这一战争罪行展开。演唱者Marichka是一位往返于加拿大与乌克兰之间的歌手，她召集了两组音乐人——一组在加拿大由全女性组合Daughters of Donbas组成，另一组则留在乌克兰本土，其中包括曾被掳走后又返回的马里乌波尔少女Lisa，她在双陶笛上贡献了一段独奏。专辑曲目在传统与原创之间交替，以弓弦乐器、班杜拉琴和钢琴为主要配器，人声从温柔转向激烈。歌词多取材于古老民歌文本，将历史上被送往异乡劳作的女孩命运与当下被劫掠的儿童处境并置，形成跨越时空的呼应。整体制作强调声乐表现力与原真性，未见明显电子或实验元素，但地域文化视角鲜明。

According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / freestyle rap
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自芝加哥南区的田野录音作品，录制地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家前廊，毗邻中途机场降落航线之下。二十五名枪支暴力幸存者参与录制，年龄跨度从十七岁至六十七岁，包括freestyle说唱与即兴讲述。制作人Ian Brennan强调所有声音均为现场实录，无任何后期音乐添加，背景中蚊虫声与社区环境音构成原始声景。参与者来自同一街区，几乎人人以不同方式卷入暴力事件——无论作为承受者或施加者。项目收益将捐赠给Cure Violence Global组织。专辑延续了Brennan此前在马拉维、卢旺达等地开展的田野录音项目路线，以声音档案形式记录被主流叙事忽视的社群经验，介于声音艺术与社会文献之间。

items.excerpt: Juri Seo thrives in the balance of complex compositional processes and aesthetic bliss. items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇对作曲家Juri Seo的访谈式介绍，聚焦于她的创作理念与作品解析。文中以她2016年的作品More Semi Simple Variations为例，分析她如何将Milton Babbitt全序列主义的"耀眼表面"重构为穿越宽松和声与音色场域的多风格漫游。这种将严谨的序列主义体系与松散的美学体验相结合的手法贯穿于她的作品目录，使其音乐具有一种即时可感的熟悉感。文章属于问答式乐评，篇幅较短，仅提供概述性信息，缺乏对具体声音细节或作品结构的深入评述，适合作为了解这位艺术家的入门导引。

items._cn_summary: Modulisme 第 146 期聚焦法国电子音乐人 Patrice Curtillat 的项目 Poborsk。这张作品以模块化合成器为核心，但并非追求精致光滑的电子建筑结构，而是刻意利用系统的不稳定性——不断变化的节奏、微小的机械式动作、织体之间的冲突，以及允许系统以不可预测的方式自行运作。在随附访谈中，Curtillat 讲述了他从盒式磁带多轨录音与吉他逐步走向模块化领域的路径。作为 Modulisme 系列的一员，发行面向小众实验听众，强调过程性与声音探索本身，而非成品化的音乐结构。整体偏向即兴式的电子实验，声音策略偏向低保真与未完成感。

items.body: Helen Linda’s Head Ahoy! Liz Harris of Grouper draws up the anchor of her 2013 slowcore side project and sets sail once more with drummer Jed Bindeman on the high seas Linda's Head by Helen On 27th March 1980 Mt. St Helens erupted. Two months later, Liz Harris (AKA Grouper) was born. In 2013, she teamed up with drummer Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmon on bass, introducing the world to their shoegaze band Helen with the double A-side single ‘Felt This Way’ / ‘Dying All The Time’. Their dreamy debut The Original Faces followed two years after with the band subsequently laying dormant… until now. The reappearance of this Pacific Northwest slowcore trio a decade later is less an eruption, more a profusion. Or, better... The post Helen – Linda’s Head appeared first on The Quietus.
