items.body: Review by Andis — Here's a record that deserves a lot more love. We Never Lost Control is one of those albums Igenuinely enjoy, and every spin leaves me in a better mood than before. After all, what's the pointof music if it doesn't entertain you and put a smile on your face?This album will never be mentioned in the same breath as the undisputed giants of progressive rock,but that hardly matters. It's a record I keep coming back to, and one I enjoy tremendously. Germanoddballs Nine Days Wonder, a band that seemed determined to reinvent themselves with every release,followed up their wonderfully bizarre debut by making a complete stylistic U-turn. The result is analbum that's surprisingly difficult to pin down.If I had to try, I'd place it somewhere between David Bowie and Van der Graaf Generator, with atouch of Genesis and Nektar sprinkled on top. What they play could broadly be called progressiverock, but that's only part of the story. There's glam rock swagger, flashes of krautrock, bursts ofhard rock, hints of jazz rock, and all of it fronted by a wonderfully (!) theatrical vocalist. Inother words, this album stubbornly refuses to sit in a single genre box.The band's greatest strength is its energy. Driven by swirling organs and keyboards, backed by aheavy and aggressive bass, they charge through inventive progressive rock that somehow manages tocombine the punch of hard rock with the structure of prog and the occasional hook of melodic pop-rock. Had I not known they were German, I would have guessed they were British without hesitation.Side A is a thoroughly enjoyable affair, filled with melodic songs that contain just enoughprogressive trickery to keep things interesting. But it's on Side B that the real fun begins. Herethe band completely lets loose, delivering colorful, adventurous prog rock with the magnificentnine-minute epic "We Grasp the Naked Meat" as the undisputed centerpiece.We Never Lost Control is a lovable little gem of an album: quirky, energetic, unpretentious, andendlessly entertaining. Think of it as a bag of mixed candy for progressive rock fans. Maybe itisn't a masterpiece, but it's the sort of record that reminds you why digging through the lesser-known corners of the genre can be so rewarding.
items._genre: crossover prog / hard rock / glam rock / krautrock
items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的德国前卫摇滚专辑风格难以归类，融合了华丽摇滚的舞台感、硬摇滚的冲击与少许爵士与krautrock色彩。旋转的管风琴与键盘构成驱动力，搭配厚重贝斯线，制造出既有前卫结构又具旋律钩子的混血声响。评论者将其置于David Bowie与Van der Graaf Generator之间，兼有Genesis式的奇思与Nektar般的流行质感。A面以旋律化曲目为主，B面则完全释放，九分钟长篇作品成为最具冒险精神的亮点。整体呈现出一种不拘一格、精力充沛且拒绝被单一标签定义的气质。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — This is from my blog "Scott's Song by Song Spotlights" with links for listening and purchasing.Clicked 5, but really a 4.5...4 is too low!T.A.P are a progressive rock band led by composer/keyboardist Michael Jobborn. On their first album, which I have not heard (2023's "Paradigms") the band was rounded out by Warr-guitarist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Cook (Phase of Twilight and others) and Guitarist/Vocalist/multi-instrumentalist Suzi James (Fearful Symmetry, whose wonderful latest album "I've Started?So I'll Finish" is reviewed on this blog as well!). Paul Sears and Bill Bachman were both contributors on the first album on the drum throne. This time around Bill Bachman is a full member. Bill is renowned for his work as a drumming educator, including his work with several Drum Corps around the US. (DCI- Drum Corps International- is a deep rabbit hole that I have been familiar with since my college days!) But his prog resume is impressive as well: (From the press release) "Bill is the drummer for Herd of Instinct, Spoke of Shadows, has toured with progressive rock artist Neal Morse, is on recordings with Trey Gunn (King Crimson), Colin Edwin (Porcupine Tree), Adam Holzman (Miles Davis & Steven Wilson), and Gerald Albright (Grammy award winning saxophonist)". So, the musical talent in this band is absolutely staggering!This album comes courtesy of Anne-Claire Rallo of Bad Dog Promotions. As always, I receive no additional compensation and am free to "call it like I hear it". In fact, when I received the email offering this review to me from Anne-Claire, I replied, "You had me at Suzi James". The album "Paradigms II" is to be released on October 3, 2026, on the Prog Rock Essentials label (Ordering info follows the review). As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Time to dig into the music!T.A.P are:Michael Jobborn - concepts, keysMark Cook - Warr guitar, bass, 12-string guitar, synth, sitar, strings, choirSuzi James - acoustic/electric guitars, keys, flute, violinBill Bachman - drums, percussionAdditional Contributors on tracks:2. Chris Gill - guitarChris Messina - synth4. Steve Bonino - guitar, lyrics/vocals5. Gayle Ellett - mellotron, acoustic/electric guitars6. Massimo Pieretti - piano, synthGayle Ellett - bouzouki, mellotron8. Tenk van Dool - mandolin, guitarChris Gill - guitarTrack 1 - Galaxy Unknown (4:28)An organ riff, accented with drums starts us off with an odd meter. The rest of the band soon joins in. There is a guitar solo after around 45 seconds. A softer section follows with alternating acoustic and electric instruments in the spotlight. This is a wonderful instrumental musical journey with many layers. As one might expect, the talent level here is through the roof! A terrific opener!Track 2 - A Beacon of Light (12:17)This one fades in with some guitar effects and synth tones. It feels like the first rays of sunlight at dawn, matching the title. Electric piano chords bring a sense of rhythm. The bass line provides melodic movement. The chords are layered among many instruments, giving a rich tonal palate. This is moving at a moderately slow tempo and a relaxed feel. The guitar solo that happens at around the 4-minute mark brings a balance of melodicism and complexity. A droning section after that leads to an upbeat groove on the bass and drums. It begins to take on a jazz fusion flavor. Synth and guitar solos float over the top of the rhythm bed. Just before 7:30 things calm down and a new section begins. Sitar sounds are a part of the soundscape. Bill's marching band experience shows in his snare part. At 8:45 we are down to lead guitar, bass and keys. The drums subtly return. We are in a slower 6-8 at this point. At 9:55 a more strident beat that reminds me of old TV themes takes over. There are so many moods in this piece; I love it! At 11:30, it reminds me of how it began. What an absolutely fantastic instrumental piece of music!Track 3 - A Dramatic Interlude (4:06)Electric piano, bass and lead guitar start this off. The drums enter a moment later. This is in a moderately slow 6-8, so far, but the title tells me something is going to happen. The tempo increases slightly and becomes more rhythmic after a small crescendo. I believe that is the Warr guitar taking the solo that follows. I love the staccato bass and guitar riff at around 2:20. Things begin to build up at around 3:20. The track ends with a long, sustained chord. A wonderful piece, but not as dramatic as the title indicated. Track 4 - A Hole in the Ground (6:14)Rich electric piano chords and clean guitars start us off here. Lead guitar emerges. And then--Vocals! Guest musician Steve Bonino is on this track with guitars and vocals. (This is not the first time his name has appeared in one of my reviews!) The drums begin to emerge as we progress. Mark Cook's basslines are fantastic on this album. Steve's voice seems a little buried in the mix at times. The drums might be a little too far back at times, as well. I like the song, but I don't feel like it's mixed as well as it could be. It would benefit from a better presentation. It ends with droning sounds.Track 5 - 4th Dimensional Wave (11:50)Sound effects fade in and guitars join. This starts out sounding like some sort of alarm. Soon, though, the music gets melodic with a fantastic guitar solo; I believe it is Suzi James. We are in a moderately slow tempo. The keys are playing a mellotron style chorus behind the solo. Some intricate rhythmic patterns follow. This keeps building, slowly and gradually. At around 4:20 we get into odd meters. At 5:45, the rhythm shifts into a different groove. I am really enjoying this one! There are tons of changes! Gayle Ellet of Djam Karet and his band the Electromags adds his keyboard abilities to the soundscapes. Probably my favorite track, so far.Track 6 - Lyrical Paradox (3:50)This one has a bit of a swing to it. Sort of a mellow melodic tune. The sound gets bigger just after the one-minute mark. Great melodies in this one. I love the slide guitar in it; it reminds me of the slide guitar in "And You and I" from Yes. This is a nice little piece. Ellet is back with bouzouki on this, and Massimo Pieretti (whom I have reviewed as well) adds keyboards.Track 7 - Outlooks of the Closed-Minded (6:29)This opens with some accents and jazz chords. It has a fusion feel to my ears. I love the syncopated rhythms. It reminds me of the Dixie Dregs a bit. Lots of melodies wind their way through this one. Wonderful track!Track 8 - Wishful Solitude (:)This one is more up-tempo, yet lighthearted. As with most of the album, the melodies are abundant! At around 3:15 Suzi plays her flute. There are many interesting things in the soundscape. At just be for the 5-minute mark, a descending synth part that sounds like the 70s idea of a UFO landing takes over, then we get a bit funky! At around 6:45 we get a psychedelic organ sound. This is a very cool piece with many different things going on. Tenk van Dool (who I am not familiar with) plays the mandolin at around 8:45. The melodies intertwine as we approach the ending. This is a wonderfully arranged prog instrumental. Great way to end this wonderful album.OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:I really liked that a lot! Unfortunately, I am not sure what happened on track 4, "A Hole in the Ground". I have always liked Steve Bonino's contributions, and he always seems to be a good guy in the online interactions I have had with him, but something just didn't work for me on that track. Otherwise, this is a fantastic album of mainly instrumental prog with some fusion tendencies. I give this a 4.5 out of 5 or 90%. Recommended!
items._genre: eclectic prog / progressive rock / fusion
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以键盘为核心的前卫摇滚作品，乐手阵容兼具Warr吉他、多种传统乐器与现代合成器，编制上呈现出强烈的跨界倾向。曲目中融入了西塔琴、锡塔尔琴、曼陀林、布祖基琴等来自不同文化传统的乐器，配合mellotron与电子音效，使整体音色在交响前卫的框架中带有世界音乐与现代古典的影子。评论者强调编曲层次丰富，开篇即以奇数拍和管风琴riff展开，强调乐手演奏技术的扎实。然而文章在音乐创新性与实验深度上的探讨有限，更多停留在乐手履历介绍与制作规格层面，未深入分析作品的独特视角或对前卫美学的推进意义。整体属于技术过硬但前卫突破性表达相对温和的折衷前卫之作。

items.album: DROWNING STEPS The Bravery of a Tireless Mind: Book One (Crossover Prog, 2026)

items.body: Review by bandtutu — Drowning Steps - The Bravery of a Tireless Mind: Book One1. The Angels and the PlaygroundThe Angels and the Playground is an excellent introduction to the album. I really like the way it begins to develop the character's story. One detail I particularly love is the sound of the pencil writing on paper. It may seem like something simple, but it really adds to the immersion in the narrative. Caio's vocals also deserve praise, as they fit the song's concept very well and help convey the emotions behind the story.The first three minutes are beautiful. The acoustic guitar is very well crafted, and the atmosphere at the beginning reminds me of moments from "The Moon Touches Your Shoulder" by Porcupine Tree and "A Pillow of Winds" by Pink Floyd. There is a nostalgic tranquility to this introduction that I really enjoy, with a delicate arrangement that allows each element to find its own space. The song progresses naturally, without rushing, and never becomes tedious.Around 4:15, we get an incredible transition. The guitar riff, accompanied by the keyboards and synthesizers, changes the whole dimension of the composition and creates one of the first major moments of the song. I really like how these elements complement each other. The acoustic guitar picking that comes in here, breaking up the rhythm, also deserves praise.At 6:30, the distorted guitar introduces a section that, although I understand its importance to the narrative and the character's emotional context, buy simply doesn't work for me. I really don't like the riff. I understand the intention behind the change and recognize its purpose within the song, but I feel another approach could have conveyed the same feeling in a better way. It's a very personal criticism, especially because the composition wins me back shortly afterward.At 7:37, another guitar riff comes in, accompanied by the synthesizer, and the result is excellent. The drums also deserve praise, as the changes in the groove give the composition more personality. I really like the bass's rich and distinctive tone, and for me, this combination works so well that it makes up for much of what bothered me in the previous section.At 9:07, after a very striking, almost ghostly break, the song moves into a section that reminds me of "Moonloop" by Porcupine Tree. Even though this is a relatively long passage, it never becomes tedious. The instrumental development keeps me interested and shows the band's ability to sustain extended sections without simply relying on the repetition of the same idea.At 10:47, a riff with a more metal feel begins to emerge. I can't quite define exactly what kind of sound it is, but I really like the change. It's the kind of riff I would even like to write myself, both because of its sound and the energy it carries. Just a few seconds later, at 11:02, another transition completely changes the emotional state of the song. The arrangement takes on a different dimension, setting the stage for one of my favorite moments of the track.The keyboards entering at 11:23 are simply incredible. The piano comes in with a very emotional quality, adding a special sensitivity to everything that had been building up until that point. This section really moved me, especially because of the way the instrument transforms the atmosphere without needing an exaggerated change in intensity. Thiago's work on the keyboards is fundamental here, showing how important his contributions are to the musical identity of both the song and the album.When everything seems to be heading toward a satisfying conclusion, the guitar comes back and creates a sudden shock that, interestingly enough, works very well for me. I don't see this choice as a problem, in fact, I really like the effect it creates.However, my biggest criticism comes right after that, at 12:27, when the previously used riff returns. I feel that bringing it back is unnecessary and slightly hurts the flow of the composition. In my opinion, the song had already found an interesting path toward its conclusion, and I didn't like going back to that idea.Still, I really like the grandiose effect created by the keyboards together with the vocals during the "Then we went up, then we went down" section. The combination has a lot of strength and fits the scale of the narrative, although the repetition of this passage became a little boring for me. The ending of the section, with the guitar delay, works well and sets the stage for the final part of the song.The final section is beautiful. After so many changes in intensity and instrumental passages, the song finally reaches a sense of peace that almost feels like a release. The atmosphere reminds me a lot of "Insurgentes" by Steven Wilson. It also gives me the same feeling of relief I get when "Raider II" ends and "Like Dust I Have Cleared from My Eye" begins on Grace for Drowning. After such a long emotional journey, it feels like you can finally breathe.Despite some choices that don't completely work for me, "The Angels and the Playground" is a very strong opening, with excellent instrumental moments, engaging dynamic shifts, and an atmosphere that contributes just as much to the musical experience as it does to the narrative.------------------------------------2. Fragments of a LifetimeI found this song quite interesting, especially because it takes a very different approach from the previous track. It has this kind of progressive folk-ballad feel, with a very atmospheric arrangement. The keyboard effects also remind me a lot of "Entangled" by Genesis, and I think they fit the song really well.I also really liked the ending, when the song starts to give you the feeling that something is going wrong. It's an interesting choice because it works as a lead-in to the next track, "The Nod", leaving a certain sense of tension in the air.I like the idea behind the lyrics, especially this moment where the character is searching for peace. Overall, it's a simple track, but it works really well within the story of the album. --------------------------3. The NodThe beginning of this song reminds me a lot of Opeth atmosphere. Then a very distinctive guitar riff comes in. I wouldn't necessarily say it's good or bad, but I understand the idea behind it and I think it works.I really like the part around 2:35, when a sequenced drum pattern starts playing in the background. I thought that was a very interesting choice, and it reminds me of some things Wilson has done. The drums also deserve some praise here; they give the song a lot of dynamics and help build that sense of tension without simply making everything heavy all the time.The bass solo is also really good, especially with the character's narration playing in the background. Then the heavy guitar riff from the beginning comes back, and this time I think it really gains more meaning and fits the song very well.I also really liked the synthesizer solo, which brings a different texture to the track. The guitar solo is good as well and works nicely within the composition.Overall, I think the song takes its time to show this depth and develop the idea further.----------------------------------------------4. Waiting for RedemptionThis is easily my favorite song on the album. It starts with a piano in the background and Caio's vocals, which once again deserve a lot of praise. I really like how the song gradually builds along with the lyrics, creating more and more tension as it progresses.The way the song keeps building gives me a strong Neal Morse vibe. I can't really say whether it reminds me more of Transatlantic, Spock's Beard, or his solo work, but there is definitely something about the way the song develops that makes me think of those bands.Around 3:50, a guitar riff comes in and fits the song really well. The effects also deserve a lot of praise here. They manage to create a completely different atmosphere and then return to the previous one in a very natural way, without making the transitions feel forced.This particular riff really reminds me of a riff from the bridge of "Weenie Beenie," from Foo Fighters first album. It's not exactly the same, of course, but the way the riff comes in gives me a very similar feeling.Then, around 5:15, the song goes through a complete change. Once again, it shifts into a darkness and more introspective atmosphere.Shortly after that, the synthesizer solo comes in, and together with the drums, it sounds incredible. Listening to it gives me a really good feeling, almost as if I'm going on a trip. And maybe that's exactly what the character is experiencing in the story as well.Then that heavy riff comes back, this time accompanied by a wah-wah guitar solo, and I absolutely love it. It's really spectacular. The combination of the riff, the guitar tone, and the wah-wah works incredibly well.A new verse then comes in, very well placed, followed by the return of that almost ghostly section, which keeps repeating.My only real criticism is that this final part starts to feel a repetitive. I like the atmosphere it creates, but I think it goes on a little longer than it should.Even so, this is easily the track that stands out the most to me. It has so many great ideas that fit together really well, and the way it moves between different atmospheres while maintaining the narrative is excellent.----------------------------5. Life Handed Me the MapThis is the song that closes the album. It feels like the character is expressing his gratitude for having finally found the path; the "map", that will allow him to reconnect with the fragments of his past.I really like the effects and the atmosphere of the song. There is something very calm and reflective about it, which makes it feel appropriate as the ending of the story.I also really like the detail of hearing him write again at the end of the song, followed by the sound of the book closing. I think it's a great way to bring the album to an end, especially because the sound of the pencil writing appeared earlier in the story. It gives the whole thing a feeling of closure, almost as if we've just finished reading the character's story ourselves.--------------Overall Opinion on the AlbumFor me, this is a work that shows how much the band has matured, both in their songwriting and in the way they tell their story. I really enjoyed the songs, especially the way the album manages to create different atmospheres and make them work within the narrative.The main highlights for me were The Angels and the Playground, The Nod, and especially Waiting for Redemption. Overall, this is an album that really surprised me and shows how much Drowning Steps has evolved. It's a record I definitely plan to listen to over and over again, because I feel like there are still a lot of details to discover.-----------My Ratings:4,3/5 8,6/10Congratulations for this excellent work.Caio Claro / vocals, acoustic guitar (1), guitars (2,5), Arrangements and Sound ManipulationFabricio Mendon�a / drumsLeonardo Gon�alves / bassMarcos Duran / guitars (1-4)Tiago Pierucci / keyboards, synthesizers, effects, organ, piano, Wah-Wah guitar (2), backing vocals (4), Arrangements and Sound ManipulationRobin Peachey / vocals (1)La�s Gonzalez / vocals (2)Erlend Viken / vocals (3)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以叙事概念为核心，开篇以铅笔书写纸面的音效营造沉浸感，声学吉他引出怀旧氛围，与Porcupine Tree及Pink Floyd的宁静段落有相似气质。作品在推进过程中多次通过吉他riff与合成器的组合实现情绪转折，从内省过渡到更具冲击力的金属化段落，并在长篇器乐发展中保持张力。评论者对部分失真吉他段落的处理持保留意见，认为旋律选择未能完全契合叙事意图，但随后被更精致的编曲与鼓点变化重新打动。整体而言，专辑在结构编排与情绪层次上展现了较强的构建能力，融合了原声质感、合成器氛围与金属元素，但评论更偏向传统前卫摇滚的叙事手法，在实验性与声音设计的突破上较为有限。

items.body: Kontravoid released his new album “Sound Of The Void” on 2 October 2026 via Artoffact Records. The ten-track release is Cameron Findlay’s second full-length for the Toronto label, following 2024’s “Detachment.” Coldwave, EBM and electro run through the record. Side-Line covered the album’s announcement in September, when “Without” arrived as the first advance track. “Mortal” and “Chances” followed ahead of the full release. Sound Of The Void by Kontravoid The tracklist runs “Sound Of The Void,” “Without,” “Mortal,” “Subject,” “Chances,” “Dimension,” “Forever,” “Abandon,” “Returning” and “Phantom.” “Sound Of The Void” is available digitally and on CD, with a clear-vinyl first pressing also available on Bandcamp. About Kontravoid Kontravoid is the solo project of Canadian musician and producer Cameron Findlay, now based in Los Angeles. Before starting Kontravoid, he played drums with Crystal Castles in 2007 and 2008 and was a founding member of Toronto synth-pop band Parallels. His self-titled Kontravoid debut followed in 2012, released through the Minimal Wave label. He has toured North America alongside Buzz Kull, and the mask he wears on stage has become part of the project’s identity, a presence carried into “Sound Of The Void.”
items._genre: coldwave / EBM / electro / darkwave / synth-pop
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是加拿大音乐人Cameron Findlay以Kontravoid名义发行的第二张全长作品，透过Artoffact厂牌推出。整张唱片围绕冷波、工业电子与电子舞曲的脉络展开，十首曲目从标题来看偏向虚无、遗弃、幻影等抽象意象，营造出冷峻疏离的氛围。作为单人项目，Findlay延续了自2012年同名首作以来的面具舞台美学，将视觉符号与音乐主题统一在一种身份隐匿的状态下。他早年曾参与Crystal Castles鼓手工作并是Parallels的创始成员，电子制作经验深厚。专辑以CD、透明黑胶和数字形式发行，限量首版在Bandcamp售卖，整体定位偏向独立暗潮场景而非主流市场。

items.body:
Stick Men are bringing their progressive rock explorations to Singapore.

The trio comprising Tony Levin, Pat Mastelotto, and Markus Reuter will perform at Singtel Waterfront Theatre on 29 January 2027 at 8PM. Presented by LAMC Presents, Tony Levin Stick Men – Live in Singapore will showcase the band’s unconventional instrumentation and intricate, rhythm-driven sound.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by L.A.M.C. (@lamcpresents)

Formed in 2007, Stick Men build their music around Levin’s Chapman Stick, Reuter’s 8-string Touch Guitar, and Mastelotto’s mix of acoustic and electronic percussion. Using two-handed tapping techniques, the string players weave together bass lines, melodies, and layered textures, giving the three-piece a sound that stretches well beyond a traditional rock trio.

Levin is best known for his longstanding work with King Crimson and Peter Gabriel, alongside recording and touring credits with artists including John Lennon, David Bowie, and Pink Floyd. Fellow King Crimson member Mastelotto, who co-founded Mr. Mister, brings loops, samples, and electronic textures into his drumming, while Reuter draws on a background spanning progressive rock, electronic music, and contemporary composition.

The Singapore date follows the September release of Let’s THRAK Again, the trio’s tribute to King Crimson’s 1995 album THRAK. Stick Men are touring the record across North and South America, Europe, and Asia, adding to a live history of more than 500 concerts in over 40 countries.

Tickets will be available via LAMC Presents, with sale details as follows:

LAMC members’ pre-sale: 7 October, 12PM SGT. Tickets priced at SGD98, SGD108, SGD118, and SGD128, with limited availability.

General sale: 8 October, 12PM SGT. Tickets priced at SGD98, SGD108, SGD128, and SGD138.

items.body: Megiapa Intentions LA-based artist is adventurous and experimental, still emanating warmth Intentions by megiapa Born out of a period of change and movement, Intentions is a debut album that acts as a snapshot of producer, vocalist and visual artist Megiapa’s journey over the past couple of years. Featuring expressive grooves, mellow textures and an array of guest appearances from the likes of The Growth Eternal, pianist Ahmad Muhammad aka Kafari, and drummer Mekala Session, Intentions is a quietly confident collection that maps a multitude of experiences, from heartbreak to healing. Album opener ‘Open Your Eyes’ provides an alluring introduction, as a slap-bass sound welcomes you to the record’s soundscape, Megiapa’s soft voice and velvety vocal delivery enveloped by soulful harmonies. As it ends, the track... The post Megiapa – Intentions appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: experimental / electronic / soul / vocal
items._cn_summary: Megiapa的首张专辑《Intentions》诞生于一段变动与迁徙期，记录了她作为制作人、歌手与视觉艺术家的心路历程。专辑邀请The Growth Eternal、钢琴家Ahmad Muhammad（Kafari）与鼓手Mekala Session等客座音乐人参与，呈现出流畅律动与柔和质感的交织。开场曲《Open Your Eyes》以slap bass音色构建声音空间，其柔和的人声与丝绒般的演唱被灵魂和声包裹。整张作品以低调的自信呈现，从心碎到疗愈的多元情感体验在音乐中徐徐展开。作为洛杉矶独立音乐人，Megiapa将温暖的灵魂气质与冒险的实验态度融为一体，体现出多媒介艺术家的整体创作视角。

items.album: Svaj. remixes alan is waiting single ‘where you disappear’

items.body: Swedish duo Svaj. released a remix of the alan is waiting track “where you disappear” on 2 October 2026. The one-track single, titled “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild),” streams on Spotify and is available for download on Bandcamp and Subvert. The original song was written and sung by alan is waiting, the recording name of a Stockholm-based electronic artist whose debut album, “The Last of You,” came out in 2024. Svaj., the duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg based in Blackeberg, Stockholm, reworked the track for the remix. The release keeps alan is waiting’s original vocals. In a newsletter announcement, Svaj. described the result as “a wonky, New Order-tinged full-on synth-pop hit song.” where you disappear – Svaj. rebuild by Svaj., alan is waiting A visualizer for “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” is available on YouTube. About Svaj. Svaj. is the Stockholm duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg, based in the Blackeberg district of the city. The duo releases through its own TZW Produktion imprint. Svaj.’s Bandcamp profile describes its sound as “voice, electronics and bass. Minimal, experimental and industrial, yet melodic and danceable,” and compares it to Joy Division and Front 242. Svaj. issued its debut EP, “Rewind,” in March 2022. The songs reworked tracks originally recorded on tape in 1988, revisited with a Yamaha CS-10 synthesizer and a 1960s Tandberg reel-to-reel recorder. The duo’s second release, “Until We Fall,” followed in 2023. In 2024, Svaj. released the single “Cut Me Up,” a reworking of a song first written by Alien Waveform in 1989 and later issued as “Contagion” on the 1993 compilation “Tapping the Wires (A Selection of Futuristic Electro Mindbeats).” The digital single included a remix by UK industrial act Portion Control. The same year, Svaj. contributed “Brända Barn,” a reworking of a 1980 Swedish punk song, to the six-act compilation “SVÄRTA.” Svaj. released its third collection, “Maggots,” a six-track release, on 17 May 2025 through TZW Produktion on vinyl, CD and digital formats. The record includes a cover of John Cale’s 1974 track “Fear Is a Man’s Best Friend” and features contributions from Perra Wikström on contrabass and guitar and vocal effects from Devoid. Svaj. issued four music videos from “Maggots” through 2025, for “Experience,” “Fear,” “Portent” and, in October 2025, “Piglet.” The duo released the single “Patterns” on 19 February 2026. Svaj.’s catalog now runs from the 2022 “Rewind” EP through this month’s “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” remix.

Rebuild)》，原曲来自Stockholm电子艺术家alan is waiting。Svaj.由Anders O Öhgren与Tomas Z Westberg组成，作品以人声、电子与贝斯为核心，自述风格介于极简、实验、工业与旋律化、舞曲之间，常被比作Joy Division与Front 242。混音保留了原曲人声，被描述为带有New Order色彩的合成器流行作品。Svaj.此前通过自家厂牌TZW Produktion发行多张作品，包括重新演绎1988年磁带录音的首张EP，以及对John Cale 1974年曲目的翻唱。文章作为新闻资讯，仅提供发行信息与背景介绍，缺乏对混音作品音乐性、技术处理或艺术价值的深度评析。

items.body: Raveiac, a new rave-punk project from Turkey, released the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1” on SoundCloud on 2 October 2026. The five-track set gathers “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” tagged as techno on the platform. The compilation is part of a wider opening catalog. Raveiac released five tracks on 2 October: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It.” Two more, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit,” followed on 3 October, and “Backstall” closed the run on 4 October, for eight tracks in three days. There is no Bandcamp page yet. The catalog streams exclusively through Raveiac’s SoundCloud profile. Raveiac’s own description connects the project to “industrial rave, hard techno, breakbeat, EBM, gabber and digital hardcore,” through what it calls “a direct punk vocabulary: repeated commands, physical hooks and lyrics shaped by concrete rooms, surveillance, machinery, appetite and loss of control.” The project’s SoundCloud bio reads in full: “Rave-punk from Turkey. Dirty industrial raves, broken breaks, and digital decay. Repost what hits. Push it deeper underground.” ‘Rust & Strobe’ and ‘Swallow the Noise’ Raveiac singled out two tracks from the set for press attention. “Rust & Strobe” opens on metallic percussion and broken drums and closes on what the project calls “an acid-charged chorus.” “Swallow the Noise” is described as a faster industrial-rave track carried by a chanted vocal line and distorted production. Raveiac also presents a visual identity drawn from photocopied zines, neon imagery, torn paper, halftone noise and analog damage. About Raveiac Raveiac launched in October 2026 as an independent rave-punk project from Turkey. Between 2 and 4 October 2026, the project released eight tracks on SoundCloud: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It” on 2 October, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit” on 3 October, and “Backstall” on 4 October. Five of those tracks, “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” make up the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1”.

items.body: Toronto-based guitarist, Ayal Senior, developed an approach of listening, playing and collaborating deeply, unhurried and with space (hence the title ‘Yutori‘, which translates to ‘space’) after several creative sojourns to Japan. This philosophy of taking time and patience to create comes through the record’s immeansly laid-back and tranquil dream-folk vibes. The album grew out of of a hushed winter morning session in the recording studio with Senior and several of his friends and collaborators leaning into this almost zen-like method of playing and being in tune with each other. The music’s vast openness and meditative qualities reflect the nature of these sessions, giving them the loose and communal feeling of tight improvised jams. This cooperative energy gives the record a sense of excitement, as it gives the impression the songs can go into any direction at any time. So your ear and attention are hooked right away, and they remain held til the needle reaches the deadwax on Side B. Throughout the album, you are treated to unique variations of instrumental ambient folk that splinters into cosmic string music and astral Americana sounds, with spacey pedal steel, acoustic and fried electric guitar, pearly vibraphones and warm cello. Some tracks are like mini-baroque symphonies, while others lean more into the psychedelic, with dreamlike atmospheric passages and stream of consciousness-styled distorted soloing. The record has the ambiance of a Nick Drake LP, but paired with the looseness and cosmic expansiveness of a Matt Valentine or even a Popol Vuh album. This is especially true with the track that finishes out Side A, “Well of Seven.” Yutori is as serene as a day spent floating around in a still pond, as pastoral as a walk through a freshly snow-covered forest and as illusory and wistful as a half-remembered daydream. If you need a bucolic and peaceful listen to soundtrack your autumn, then this is the album you should reach for. Click here to get your copy on vinyl or digital today. -KH

items._cn_summary: 多伦多吉他手Ayal Senior在多次旅日后将日式"余裕"哲学注入创作，以安静从容的态度与多位合作者在冬日录音室中完成即兴式的合奏。整张专辑呈现出极为松散而开放的氛围，大量留白与冥想质感贯穿始终，乐器配置涵盖原声吉他、电吉他、踏板钢棒琴、颤音琴与大提琴，音色交织出宇宙感的弦乐群像与迷幻民谣的漂浮感。部分段落接近巴洛克室内乐的精致编织，另一些则滑入意识流式的失真独奏。评论将其与Nick Drake的宁静气质及Matt Valentine、Popol Vuh的宇宙广袤并置。整体偏向梦幻民谣与迷psychedelic氛围的融合，虽触及实验即兴元素，但核心仍扎根于传统民谣语汇，对偏好实验、前卫与电子边界的听众而言创新力度有限。

items.body: Out of all of the underrated bands I know, Boss Keloid have to be among the most underrated. They have many virtues I could sing but the main one is that they just sound like no one else. Their type of winding, dense, and uniquely harmonic stoner/progressive rock is just inimitable. And so, I live between Keloid to Keloid release, craving the very specific flavor that only they can provide. Happily, my latest fix is almost here and good lord is it glorious! Float & Aperture leaves behind a lot of the size and grandiosity of Family The Smiling Thrush and the density of Melted On the Inch in favor of a hard to pin down etherealness. "Pedestal", the second track which I am very pleased to premiere here, will do a better job at explaining what I mean than I can. Check it out below. Float & Aperture by Boss Keloid God, I just love this band. On "Pedestal" you get a taste of the leitmotif which runs through the entire album, some strangely (and pleasingly) sweet, high pitched vocals, and a whole lot of that sound palette that makes Boss Keloid who they are. Which is what exactly? It's that insidious lead guitar line, the fact that I could mean any of the three (at my count) lead guitar lines, the bubbling bass, the way the whole thing feels off-kilter, hazy, and psychedelic to such a unique degree. And finally, it's the excellent lyrics, here (like on the rest of the album) turned very introverted, musing on meaning, intent, self-knowledge, and failure.The entire release is this good. Like "Pedestal", it's angry at times. At others it's alluring, fantastical, strange, self-flagellating, self-aggrandizing, and a few dozens other emotions and perspectives besides. It's similar to previous Keloid releases but also different, uniquely its own thing just like all of their other albums. God I love this band. Please listen to this band! The full thing drops on October 23rd and you can, and should, pre-order it from the Bandcamp page above.
items._genre: progressive rock / stoner rock / psychedelic
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于乐队Boss Keloid新专辑《Float & Aperture》的单曲首播评论。评论指出乐队以独特的缠绕、密集且和谐的声音质感著称，融合了迷幻与前卫摇滚元素。新作放弃了以往作品中的宏大叙事与密度，转向一种难以定义的空灵感。评论重点分析了第二首曲目《Pedestal》：多层次相互缠绕的主音吉他旋律、流动的低音线、偏高且甜美的声乐、整体呈现的不稳定与迷幻氛围。歌词聚焦于内向思考，涉及意义、意图、失败等主题。整张专辑情感光谱宽广，从愤怒到诱惑、从奇幻到自我鞭策，延续乐队辨识度的同时又自成一格。专辑于10月23日正式发行。

items._cn_summary: 挪威音乐人尼尔斯·佩特·莫尔维尔延续其ECM时期的近未来声响美学，推出与多位国际艺术家合作的新专辑。参与阵容横跨电子与摇滚领域，包括Imogen Heap、Alva Noto、Miki Yui，以及齐柏林飞艇贝斯手约翰·保罗·琼斯。专辑与同名纪录片同步制作，呈现跨媒介的创作模式。Molvær此前已有将ECM时期作品再构为现场版本的经历，此次则进一步拓展跨界协作的边界——电子音效与爵士质感在项目框架下交织。整体定位偏向艺术性合作项目，适合对实验电子与当代爵士交汇领域有兴趣的听众。

items._cn_summary: 拉普索迪时隔两年的专辑以非洲根源探寻为出发点，重新审视黑人女性身份认同与社群意识。米斯特·波特担任整体制作统筹，马德利布参与节奏设计，嘻哈基底扎实，Flow稳健有力。'Apple Juice'取样迪安杰洛的名作，呈现官能化的新灵魂乐表达；'OMG (Love To Sun Ra)'则与乔治·克林顿的念白交织，呼应桑·拉阿的非洲未来主义哲学，将远古与未来串联。专辑对黑人音乐文化的脉络梳理清晰，从新灵魂到阿弗里卡未来主义，体现出作者的文化自觉与跨界野心。作为意识说唱作品，其文本密度与社会议题意识突出，但在声音实验层面更偏向于风格拼贴而非彻底的解构或先锋探索。

On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由挪威二人组Sudan Dudan联合Hans Hulbækmo和Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard共同制作完成，以原声吉他为主导，辅以小提琴、langeleik琴、里拉琴、口簧琴等传统乐器。八首歌曲的歌词全部使用挪威语，涉及大地、太阳、月亮、星辰、失落、悲伤、神话与谜语等主题，整体情绪带有反思与忧郁的气质，但并非一味沉重。专辑在传统民谣基础上融入实验元素：一首作品借鉴并重塑法国知名旋律，加入非正统和声；另一首运用挪威特有的tralling人声技法，以纯人声取代器乐伴随舞蹈。最末曲是唯一使用电吉他的作品，深沉而带有twang音色，令人联想到Duane Eddy或David Lynch配乐。作为独立小规模发行，制作精良且富有想象力，但整体仍扎根于北欧民谣传统，跨界融合有限。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Section X" is the second full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act BeyondTwilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works of another band). The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in March 2005. It�s the successor to "The Devil's Hall of Fame"from 2001. The nucleus of the band is intact (namely keyboard player and band founder Finn Zierler,guitarist Anders Ericson Kragh, bassist Anders Lindgren, and drummer Tomas Fred�n) since the releaseof "The Devil's Hall of Fame" but there have been a couple of lineup changes. The omnipresent JacobHansen (Invocator, Anubis Gate, Pyramaze...etc.) has joined on guitars and vocals, and American leadvocalist Kelly Sundown Carpenter (Darkology, Inner Sanctum, Outworld...etc.) has replaced Norwegianvocalist J�rn Lande (Ark, Masterplan, Allen - Lande...etc.).Stylistically the material on "Section X" is a combination of epic power metal and heavy metaloriented progressive metal. The latter means that this is progressive oriented music but nottechnical for the sake of it, and you shouldn't expect long instrumental sections dominating thetracks. Beyond Twilight�s music is more song oriented and generally features relatively accessibleverse/chorus structures. The tracks are quite sophisticated though (listen to the almost theatrical"Sleeping Beauty"). The closest relative is to my ears Symphony X because of the power metal andprogressive metal hybrid style, but also because of the epic nature of the music, the heaviness ofthe music (this is not vanilla Euro power metal), and the omnipresence of keyboards. Carpenter isquite the impressive singer with a strong voice and commanding delivery and the musicianship isgenerally through the roof on this release."Section X" features a powerful, heavy, and detailed sound production. It�s polished and wellproduced but still heavy and raw enough not to become too sterile sounding. Every instrument andvocal part stand out in the mix and are perfectly balanced. Just because this is Zierler�s projectdoesn�t mean that the keyboards overshadow everything else. On the contrary Zierler is veryconscious in terms of when his keyboards should dominate a track and when they shouldn�t. Uponconclusion "Section X" is a step up in quality from the already great "The Devil's Hall of Fame" andit�s just through and through a high quality release from Beyond Twilight. A 4 - 4.5 star (85%)rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由丹麦乐队Beyond Twilight于2005年通过Massacre Records发行，是其第二张正式录音室作品。音乐风格以史诗力量金属为底色，融合重金属倾向的前卫金属，但并非以炫技为核心，而是注重歌曲本身的可听性，采用相对易入耳的主歌副歌结构。键盘在作品中占据重要地位，编曲偏向宏大叙事方向，制作精良且层次分明，鼓、贝斯、键盘与人声均获得清晰呈现。新加入的吉他手与主唱带来厚重嗓音与强烈舞台感，使整体在力量与细节之间取得平衡。相比前作在品质上有所提升，但整体仍属于力量金属框架内的稳健延续，在前卫性与实验性方面并未做出显著突破。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Few late-80s metal albums are as influential as Savatage's fourth studio offering 'Hall of theMountain King', originally released by Atlantic. This is the first album by the American bandproduced by then-new producer Paul O'Neill, who had insisted on a more coherent musical direction,while also adding a bit of a conceptual edge to their recordings. At the same time, the band shows awillingness to experiment with more sophisticated arrangements and tighter compositions, as heardthroughout the album. The result is a darker, progressive-oriented record that sits at theintersection of melodic power metal and technical heavy metal, offering a triumphant and relentlesssound graced by fast-paced guitars and stunning vocal performances. As usual, fantastical elementsprevail on this Savatage album, bringing along an interesting aesthetic that sets the band apartfrom many of its contemporaries in the heavy metal scene. The lack of success of their previousalbums may have motivated Savatage to create a solid, kind of "bulletproof" collection of songs,that is what the record feels like.The straightforward songwriting, thunderous solos, and the overall dark atmosphere of 'Hall of theMountain King' render this album an appealing listen from start to finish. Its ten tracks areprimarily written by Jon and Criss Oliva, respectively lead singer and lead guitarist of the band,while a few songs also credit producer O'Neill as a co-writer. This record also has instrumentalarrangements of excerpts from 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' by Grieg and 'Mars, the Bringer ofWar' by Holst, which is further proof that Savatage were pursuing a sophistication of their soundwith this release. Opening side one is the song '24 Hrs. Ago'. Its sweeping, metallic riff providesa menacing and theatrical tone that is taken on by the following track 'Beyond the Doors of theDark', which is another really heavy and powerful composition. 'Legions' then explores a grooved uppower metal sound, while the melodic number 'Strange Wings' sees Savatage dialing back on the speedand aggression of the first three songs. Side two then follows up with the instrumental 'Prelude toMadness' and the iconic title track that needs no introduction. Of the four songs that follow andconclude the record, 'White Witch' and 'Devastation' impress as well-arranged ballsy metal pieces,while the instrumental interlude 'Last Dawn' is quite enjoyable. Of course, many of the progressiveelements are still underdeveloped on this release, while the instrumentals occasionally feel likestopgap entries in a sequence of songs mostly dedicated to powerful riffing and vocal bravado.Nevertheless, the vocals of Jon Oliva are fantastic all throughout 'Hall of the Mountain King',while the writing and the arrangements are really strong. The quality of the entire album isindicative of how Paul O'Neill understood what the band needed to become an 80s heavy metal majesty.And despite its minor imperfections, this 1987 record remains one of the most important entries inthe band's catalogue.
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / heavy metal
items._cn_summary: 这张1987年的专辑是Savatage转向更连贯音乐方向的转折点，制作人Paul O'Neill的介入带来了概念化倾向与更精密的编曲。整体呈现出旋律力量金属与技术重金属交汇的特质，吉他riff快速推进，Jon Oliva的人声表现尤为突出。专辑融入Grieg《山魔王的宫殿》与Holst《火星》选段的器乐改编，体现出乐队对古典素材的借鉴企图。歌词与美学仍延续奇幻主题，与同期重金属场景形成差异。但专辑的前卫元素仍属初步探索，器乐段落有时更像歌曲间的过渡填充，未能真正深入实验领域。对于偏好前卫、实验与融合的音乐听众而言，这张作品的音乐语言仍偏向传统重金属框架，跨界深度有限。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — A crisp, violin and guitar led prog act can't help but invoke a certain era of a certain UK prog monarch led by ROBERT FRIPP, and this instrumental album isn't unworthy of such a parallel, but this is mostly in the distorted icy leads and the jazz inflections. With no vocals and a tendency to prefer structured jamming over improv, not to mention a folk orientation that Crimson increasingly set aside after 1972, it would be as unfair to SCARLET THREAD as it is to an obvious mentor to stretch this analogy any further. A better comparison might be Montreal's TALISMA or, originating in the HACKETT school, MR GIL/BELIEVE or HARNAKIS. Among fellow Finns, perhaps AQUAPLAN but without vocals, at least for now.As I said, this is jamming but in a disciplined and repetitive way that generally works well enough and is nothing if not appealing to prog ears, though everything seems a bit interchangeable - throw in a guitar motif, enhance with violin, maybe add flute, then move on to another violin theme, and enhance with guitar, maybe add flute, and so on. Luckily these are all well orchestrated. The opener and closer seem to hit highest on the sustainability index, along with "Siipirikon Lento" (flight of the bird with the injured wing). More would emerge in the subsequent decade, with a few dramatic changes, so this is not one of those debuts that unwittingly doubled as a swan song. Mildly recommended, but more enthusiastically for certain listener profiles.
items._genre: progressive folk / prog folk / instrumental
items._cn_summary: 这张芬兰乐队专辑以小提琴与吉他为主导，呈现出器乐化的前卫民谣风格。整张作品以结构化的即兴段落为骨架，避免完全自由的无调性探索，而是倾向于循环重复的主题变奏。评论将其与King Crimson早期作品相比较，提及了失真吉他主奏的冰冷质感与爵士化转折，但同时强调芬兰民谣根基是这张专辑区别于英式前卫的关键。编曲层次丰富，吉他动机、小提琴主题与偶尔的长笛交织，但整体结构略显可互换性，缺乏强烈突破性。评论温和推荐，认为开篇与结尾曲目最具持续性，'Siipirikon Lento'也是亮点。对于偏好实验前卫、爵士即兴与电子融合的听众而言，这张器乐民谣专辑与之距离较远，仅在部分爵士化处理与北欧地域特色上有微弱交集。

items.body: Independent Polish musician Sławek Stróżyk released the single “Tylko Ty” (“Only You”) on September 18, 2026, through distributor Crave Digital. The track places Polish-language male vocals in a synthwave/electro setting with a cyberpunk atmosphere, and explores closeness as a source of strength while the surrounding world changes. “Tylko Ty” runs 2 minutes and 47 seconds at 120 BPM. Stróżyk wrote the composition and lyrics, performed the track and handled its recording, production, mix and master himself in his home studio using Reaper. The original music and vocals involved no generative AI. “Tylko Ty” previously featured on the “Synthpop Symphony” podcast. The single is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. About Sławek Stróżyk Sławek Stróżyk is an independent musician, composer, guitarist, vocalist and producer based in Poznań, Poland, with more than twenty years of experience spanning session performance, recording engineering and sound design. His solo work brings together synthwave and electronic production with a wider interest in pop, ballads and rock. Stróżyk records in his own home studio using Reaper, taking responsibility for the complete creative and technical process from composition through to the finished master. “Tylko Ty,” released September 18, 2026, is his latest single under that approach. Stróżyk is currently working on his debut solo album, with material spanning pop, ballads, rock and synthwave, continuing the independent, self-produced method behind “Tylko Ty.”

items.body: Sydney-based producer Harry Klein released the single “Fleeting Moments” in 2026, a dark-pop track built from electronica, wave and witch house. The song centers on transience, and on learning to love what doesn’t last. “Fleeting Moments” runs 3:22 and carries a synthesized trumpet line, falsetto vocals and a glitch beat. The single adds to a run of 2026 releases that includes “Push and Pull,” “Only Ever Now,” “Dance Therapy,” “Sun Down” featuring Billsbry, “Wild Child” and “Refuge” featuring Just Jen. Klein is touring Europe with psych-jazz outfit Almost Toast and plans to release his second album, “On The Path,” in November 2026 after he returns to Sydney. Rex Pollard of Electronic Music Australia described Klein’s production in terms of the mood it builds: “It is clear to me that Klein contains excellent knowledge on formulating dystopian atmospheres with his production, encouraging listeners to exit reality and enter his dark, sinister worlds.” “Fleeting Moments” is available to stream on Spotify. About Harry Klein Harry Klein is a multidisciplinary artist based in Eora/Sydney who combines music production with visual artistry across audio/visual performances. His work moves through dark electronica, glitchy IDM beats and ambient textures. Klein released his debut album, “And Then There Was None,” in 2023. The record explores questions of relationships, community and social power, pairing experimental electronica and dance productions with melancholic pop songwriting. Three singles preceded it that year: “Running out of Time,” “Cut & Dirty” and “Accelerate,” followed later in 2023 by “Who Floats Above.” He has performed at Up Late at the Powerhouse Museum and the Brand X Artist Showcase, built an interactive sound installation at Wide Open Space Festival, played his festival debut at Waves Retreat Festival and collaborated with fashion label The Injury at Pitch Festival. Klein also works as Senior Technical Officer of Screen Arts and Photomedia at Sydney College of the Arts, where he teaches and mentors emerging artists. “Fleeting Moments” is the latest in a string of 2026 singles building toward “On The Path,” Klein’s second album, due in November 2026.

items._cn_summary: Harry Klein 来自悉尼，是一位跨界音乐人与视觉艺术家，作品融合暗黑流行、电子、合成器浪潮与巫术浩室元素。单曲《Fleeting Moments》以三分钟出头的篇幅呈现合成小号旋律、假声人声与故障节拍，主题围绕短暂易逝的事物展开。整体制作偏向建立阴沉氛围，运用合成器层叠与失真人声塑造略带反乌托邦色彩的情绪。评论人 Rex Pollard 称赞其擅长构建黑暗阴郁的声音世界。Klein 同时与 Almost Toast 乐队在欧洲巡演，并计划于 2026 年底发行第二张专辑《On The Path》。从风格描述来看，该作品融合了多种电子亚类型，但整体仍偏向暗黑流行的主流表达，实验性元素相对有限，缺乏深度的声音解构与即兴空间。

items.body:
Rolando Luna is bringing the sounds of Cuba to Singapore.

The former Buena Vista Social Club pianist will perform with his trio at Capitol Theatre on 30 November, blending Cuban musical traditions with jazz improvisation. Presented by Vamp Productions, Rolando Luna Trío: Soy Cuba… y Más! begins at 8PM, with doors opening at 7PM.

The trio’s repertoire spans original compositions, Cuban and American standards, boleros, and danzones. Fans can expect familiar melodies reworked through fresh arrangements and spontaneous exchanges, drawing on Luna’s grounding in Cuban rhythms, jazz, and classical music.

Winner of the 2007 Montreux Jazz piano competition, Luna has contributed to more than 200 albums. His career includes ten years performing with Buena Vista Social Club and two decades accompanying celebrated Cuban singer Omara Portuondo.

Luna began his musical journey at 15, studying at Havana’s Amadeo Roldán Conservatory before Portuondo selected him as an accompanist. Alongside their international performances, he has built his own body of work as a pianist, composer, and arranger.

The Singapore show is supported by the Embassy of Cuba in Singapore, with the Foundation for the Arts & Social Enterprise named as its charity beneficiary.

Early bird tickets are available until 14 October, 11:59PM SGT, with standard pricing taking effect on 15 October:

Seated, theatre-style free seating: SGD79 early bird / SGD88 standard

VIP Terrace: SGD124 early bird / SGD138 standard

Visit Vamp Productions’ event page for tickets and further details.

items.body: English post-punk band Killing Joke released their self-titled debut album, “Killing Joke,” on 5 October 1980 through E.G. Records, distributed by Polydor Records. The record turns 46 this year. Killing Joke recorded the album in August 1980 at Marquee Studios in London and produced it themselves, with Phil Harding as engineer. Drummer Paul Ferguson described the sessions as recorded live with “no overdubs to speak of.” The eight-track UK LP runs: “Requiem” “Wardance” “Tomorrow’s World” “Bloodsport” “The Wait” “Complications” “S.O.36” “Primitive” The original US pressing added “Change,” the B-side of the “Requiem” single, between “Complications” and “S.O.36.” “Wardance” came out as a single in February 1980, ahead of the album, and “Requiem” followed as a single in September 1980. The album entered the UK Albums Chart on 25 October 1980 at number 41 and later peaked at number 39. Its cover collages a photograph by Don McCullin of CS gas clashes in Derry, Northern Ireland, in 1971, designed by Mike Coles. In 2019, Pitchfork placed the album at number 9 on its list of the 33 best industrial albums of all time. “The Wait” was covered by Metallica on the 1987 “Garage Days Re-Revisited” EP and later included on “Garage Inc.,” “Primitive” was covered by Helmet in 1993, and “Requiem” was covered by Foo Fighters in 1997 as a B-side to “Everlong.” About Killing Joke Killing Joke formed in October 1978 in Notting Hill, London. Jaz Coleman (vocals, keyboards) and Paul Ferguson (drums) met in late 1978 and placed an announcement in Melody Maker in February 1979 reading “Bass, lead, to tell the killing joke, we mean it man!” Guitarist Geordie Walker and bassist Martin “Youth” Glover answered and completed the original line-up. The band released its debut EP, “Turn to Red,” as a 10-inch on 26 October 1979 on Malicious Damage, the label Killing Joke ran with graphic artist Mike Coles. Recorded in August 1979 at Gooseberry Sound in London, the EP drew airplay from BBC Radio 1’s John Peel. The “Almost Red” EP followed that November, and the single “Nervous System,” with “Turn to Red” as its B-side, came out in December 1979. Killing Joke then signed to E.G. Records for the self-titled debut album, released on 5 October 1980. The band’s next albums were “What’s THIS For…!” (1981) and “Revelations” (1982), after which Youth left the band and was replaced by Paul Raven on bass. “Fire Dances” followed in 1983 and “Night Time” in 1985, the album that carried the single “Love Like Blood” and brought the band its widest chart exposure to date. Killing Joke continued recording and touring into the 2010s with albums including “Absolute Dissent” (2010), “MMXII” (2012) and “Pylon” (2015), with Jaz Coleman and Geordie Walker as the group’s only constant members. Geordie Walker died in November 2023 at the age of 64, as Side-Line reported at the time. The band’s 1980 debut album remains the record that introduced the Killing Joke sound now marking its 46th anniversary this October.

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是对Killing Joke 1980年同名首张专辑的纪念性介绍，主要罗列了录音背景、曲目列表、封面设计来源以及后续被Metallica、Helmet、Foo Fighters翻唱的历史信息。文章并未深入分析专辑的音乐特征、制作手法或艺术价值，仅以编年史的方式陈述事实。该专辑被Pitchfork列入最佳工业专辑榜单第九位，其原始、几乎不加叠录的录音方式在当时的post-punk与工业音乐场景中具有一定实验性，封面采用北爱尔兰德里1971年催泪瓦斯冲突的照片，赋予作品强烈的政治与社会意涵。对于关注暗潮与工业音乐场景的听众而言，这张专辑是后朋克向工业过渡的早期代表作之一，但本文仅提供资讯性内容，缺乏评论深度。

items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail released the single “Vile Train” on 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The track is the first digital single from the band’s forthcoming full-length album “Infinite Fountain,” set for release on 6 November 2026 through the same French label. A video for “Vile Train” accompanies the single. Night Nail’s Brandon Robert wrote “Vile Train” after a visit to the ash-covered ruins of Pompeii, Italy, where a Roman fresco depicting an angel and a demon locked in embrace became the song’s starting point. The lyrics follow two dreamers from separate realities who meet at the edge of their daydreams, fall into an obsession, and become trapped in a psychological cage of their own making. Robert describes the result as a “sonic assault of dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago and co-produced by Night Nail in Berlin, with additional vocals and guitar by VV & the Void, the darkwave project of Berlin musician Valentina Veil. Watch the video for ‘Vile Train’ The official video for “Vile Train” is available on YouTube: Night Nail – ‘Vile Train’ (Official Video). ‘Infinite Fountain’ due 6 November “Infinite Fountain” is available for presale on Bandcamp ahead of its 6 November 2026 release through Icy Cold Records. “Vile Train” streams on Spotify. Infinite Fountain by Night Nail About Night Nail Night Nail was founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by Brandon Robert and Justin Deaktiviere. Michael Carpenter Jr. on guitar, David Cluff on bass and Bryan Panzeri on drums joined for the project’s early releases. The project is now based in Berlin, Germany. An early self-titled EP drew press, college radio and blog coverage across the US, Europe, South America and Australia. The band’s debut album, “LA Demons,” was released in July 2018 on Cleopatra Records. Its title draws on Dostoevsky’s novel “Demons.” The sophomore album, “March to Autumn,” followed on 15 October 2020 through Cold Transmission Music. Pete Burns of Kill Shelter co-produced, mixed and mastered the record. Touring and session musicians Valentina Veil, Ilja Gavrilenko and Manuel Wagner contributed additional parts. In September 2023, Night Nail released the single “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher,” the first taste of the album “Fates Explained” on Metropolis Records. The single reached the top five of the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The “Fates Explained” video single followed that November. In January 2024, the band released a video for “Cracks In My Heart,” with Luna De La Torre on vocals, and in July 2024 issued “Early Demons & Demos,” a 10th-anniversary edition of early material. “Vile Train,” released 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records, is the first single from “Infinite Fountain,” due 6 November 2026.

items.body:
Creepy Nuts brought Japanese hip-hop to the National Stadium, opening the Singapore leg of The Weeknd’s After Hours Til Dawn Tour with a set of anime favourites, club beats and turntable flourishes.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

Rapper R-Shitei and DJ Matsunaga make a compelling double act. R-Shitei packs his verses with quick, tightly controlled syllables, while Matsunaga cuts into the beats with scratches and rhythmic accents. Their sound gives the ear plenty to follow: the pace of the rapping, the shifting percussion and the hooks that emerge from all that activity.

‘Biriken’ opened the set with a bouncing Jersey club rhythm, followed by ‘Yofukashi no Uta’ and the jazzy ‘Daten’. The mood grew darker with ‘doppelgänger’ and ‘Chxxai’, whose pounding beats and electronic textures brought the selection closer to a late-night club set.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

A dedicated DJ routine gave Matsunaga the spotlight midway through. Scratching, quick cuts and beat juggling are central to his performance style, making the decks an instrument with their own rhythmic voice. The placement gave both halves of the partnership their due before the instantly recognisable ‘Bling-Bang-Bang-Born’.

From there, the duo moved through ‘Mirage’, ‘Fright’ and ‘Nidone’, saving ‘Otonoke’ for last. The DAN DA DAN opening theme was a crowd favourite, rounding off their energetic set before The Weeknd took the stage.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by Andis — Or, as it should probably have been called: The Endless Intro.Nobody needs to tell me this album is built from leftovers from previous sessions. After listeningto it, that fact practically introduces itself. In theory, recycling old material could have been agreat idea if anyone involved had possessed the energy, inspiration, or curiosity to actually dosomething interesting with it. Instead, the apparent creative process was: find some unused RichardWright keyboard recordings, sprinkle on a bit of guitar, drums, and the occasional mysteriousspaceship noise, then glue everything together and call it an album. Any questions?What makes this even more frustrating is that Pink Floyd is one of my favorite bands of all time.I've spent decades loving their music, so this isn't coming from a casual listener looking forsomething to complain about. If anything, I wanted to love this album more than anyone.Unfortunately, enthusiasm can only carry you so far when the music seems determined to driftaimlessly into the horizon.This record taught me an important life lesson: always listen before you buy. When I heard PinkFloyd were releasing a new album, I was so excited that I pre-ordered it immediately. That was amistake of truly Floydian proportions. I haven't been this bored since listening to The Final Cut.On the bright side, this album didn't make me quite as depressed, so I suppose that's progress.The Endless River is quite literally The Endless Intro. It feels like an introduction that somehowescaped containment and continued for over 52 minutes. If we're being generous, we can count thefinal track as an actual song, which brings the intro down to a mere 46 minutes. Was that song worthsitting through a 46-minute introduction? No. No, it was not.When you put the Pink Floyd name on an album, people naturally expect something resembling PinkFloyd. Not a 52-minute ambient soundscape that vaguely gestures toward Pink Floyd while offeringabsolutely nothing we haven't heard before, and usually heard done better. This is less a new albumand more a museum tour of discarded ideas.I'm giving it two stars, and that's me being charitable. There are a few pleasant moments scatteredthroughout the record, but they're buried beneath such a thick layer of mediocrity that excavatingthem feels like a part-time job.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Pink Floyd发行，主要素材取自The Division Bell时期的未完成录音，以Richard Wright的键盘即兴段落为核心，叠加少量吉他、鼓机与空间音效。整体呈现为长达52分钟的环境化氛围铺陈，结构松散、缺乏明确动机与推进力，更像被遗弃的片段拼贴而非完整作品。评论者指出，尽管Pink Floyd是其长期喜爱的乐队，但这张专辑未能提供任何新意，仅是对过往素材的低强度重复，缺乏创作上的好奇心与方向感。评论者给出了两星评价，并将其形容为52分钟的前奏加一首勉强成形的曲目。即便置于psychedelic/space rock与ambient的交集之中，评论者也认为其氛围构建流于平庸，难以与Pink Floyd早期在同类手法上的成就相比。
